Weapons, armour and bows are forged by hand at a Forging Station. You pick a recipe, load the materials, then work them with forging tools. The materials decide the item's stats and how well you work them decides its socket. At the Alloy Forge you can also invent new alloys and name them. Updated 22 Oct 2026

Right-click an Alloy Forge with a metal or wood to set the base. Add up to four different crystals the same way. Right-click the forge with a Lava Bucket to forge. The bucket is emptied and every ingredient is used up to make one alloy. A mix someone has already found always gives the same alloy, in any order. A new mix can fail, and then it gives Unusable Scrap, for everyone, from then on. Scrap can go to the Recycling Station. When a new alloy works, it's saved for the whole server with a made-up name. You have 60 seconds to rename it with /alloy name <Name>. After that, anyone can load it at a Forging Station.

Every metal and wood needs a perk from the Crafter profession. You earn points by levelling Crafter and spend them in /profile. Each perk needs the one before it. Without the perk, the station refuses the material with "You are not skilled enough". Crystals, leather, feathers, wool and Enchanted Dust need no perk. Crafter perk Points Unlocks Iron Smith 1 Iron IngotRefined Barkwood Steel Smith 2 Steel IngotRefined Maplewood Abyssalite Smith 3 Abyssalite IngotBronze IngotRefined Elderwood Mythril Smith 4 Mythril IngotRefined Demonwood Raw materials have to be turned into ingredients before a station will take them. Right-click an Ingredient Converter while holding them: the whole stack is converted and a Stat Preview shows which stats the material adds to each kind of item. You can do the same with an ingredient or alloy just to see its preview. The forging tools are made at the Tool Station (sneak and right-click a crafting table).

Command What it does Notes /alloy name <NewName> Names a new alloy you just forged. You have 60 seconds after forging it. Letters and underscores only; underscores show as spaces. The name must not already be taken.

Right-click an empty Forging Station and choose a category (Armor, Weapons or Bows), then a recipe. A station works on one recipe at a time. Right-click the station with each ingredient to load it. Recipes ask for types, such as "4 × Metal", so you choose which metal or wood goes in. Once everything is loaded, left-click the station with the forging tools. Each material needs its own amount of work from each tool, and the recipe doesn't tell you how much. Left-click with the Forging Branding Tool to finish. You can finish whenever you like after loading. Right-click with it to see your progress, or sneak and left-click to cancel. Warning Cancelling, or breaking the station mid-project, drops the loaded ingredients and loses the work. You can't break a Forging Station while holding a forging tool.

Crystals The 40 gemstones and four other crystals. Only crystals can go into an alloy. When you finish, you see your Hit Percentage: how close your work came to what the materials needed. Working too much costs as much as working too little, and only exact work can reach Masterwork. The grade decides the socket the item gets. It doesn't change the stats, which come from the materials, but your Crafter XP is scaled by the percentage. Hit Percentage Quality Socket Below 50% Rusted None 50% Tempered Basic 75% Polished Polished 90% Gleaming Radiant 100% Masterwork Mythical Mage armour gets Armor Rune sockets instead of gemstone ones (Minor, Lesser, Greater and Ascendant, at the same thresholds). Everything else takes infused gemstones.

There are 36 recipes. "4 × Metal" means any four metal ingredients: four Iron Ingots, a mix, or an alloy. The item is named after the material you used most, shown here as Material. Claim farm animals, keep them fed and clean, and breed them for better meat, milk, eggs and materials. Updated 23 Oct 2026

Breed animals with their normal Minecraft breeding food. Both parents must be grown, fed, clean and not neutered. If either parent is owned, you must own both. Wild animals start with 0 to 20 genetics and 0 care. Babies inherit genetics from their parents, with a boost that improves when the parents are well cared for. Raise both parents' care before breeding. Higher-star breeding food also helps; food with no stars gives the same benefit as 5-star food. Genetics can reach 1,000 through breeding. Babies take 1 hour to grow up (chickens 45 minutes) and look like babies until then. They have to be grown before they can breed, give milk or eggs, or drop meat. Neutering is permanent Right-click an animal you own with the Neutering Tool to stop it from ever breeding again.

An animal is happy when it is neither Hungry nor Dirty. Every 4 to 8 hours that its area is loaded, an animal becomes Hungry or Dirty, shown next to its name. Feed a hungry animal 1 Universal Feed and clean a dirty one with the Glove. Each time you do, you get a little Farming experience. Care How it works Gaining care A happy animal gains 1 care per minute while its area is loaded, up to 200. While you are away When the area unloads, a happy animal can still gain up to 8 hours' worth of care. After more than 8 hours unloaded, it is Hungry or Dirty when the area loads again. Losing care If it stays Hungry or Dirty for more than 24 hours, it loses 1 care every 10 hours, even while unloaded. Care counts whenever the area is loaded, by you or by anyone else. It does not matter whether the owner is online.

Rename an Ownership Token at an anvil to the name you want for the animal. Right-click the animal with the token. Horses and other animals that need taming must be tamed first. The token is used up. Sneak and right-click the animal with an empty hand to see its owners, care, genetics and growth. You can claim cows, pigs, sheep, goats, chickens, horses, donkeys, mules, camels and llamas. Animals belong to the character who claimed them, but the limit of 15 counts every animal on your account, shared ones included. Bees are not part of husbandry. Unclaimed animals vanish Livestock nobody owns is removed the next time its area loads, and it drops nothing if killed. Newborn cows, pigs, sheep, goats, chickens and llamas count as unowned even when both parents are yours, so claim them before you leave the pen. Wolves, cats and ocelots, tamed or not, are removed the same way and cannot be claimed. Owning an animal does not protect it from players, mobs or fire.

Command Aliases What it does Notes /animals /livestock Lists the animals your current character owns or shares, and where each was last seen. Shows each animal's name and kind, whether it is still growing, and whether it is happy, hungry or dirty, plus how many of your account's 15 places are used. Click the coordinates to copy them. If a place is missing, visit that animal once. Right-click an Animal Station to craft a Mount Whistle. Blow it with a right-click and every horse, donkey, mule, llama and trader llama within 64 blocks glows for 5 seconds, so you can spot it through walls. It finds every such animal, not only yours, and chat tells you how many answered. Camels do not answer. Other players can hear the whistle, and it has a 3-second cooldown.

Owners can ride their horses, donkeys, mules, camels and llamas. Higher genetics and care give horses, donkeys and mules more health, speed and jump. Camels and llamas are the same however well they are bred. Inspect an animal to see its stats.

Animal While alive When killed Cow Milk with a bucket every 20 minutes. Sheds leather now and then. Beef roast and leather Goat Milk with a bucket every 20 minutes. Shear for wool. Goat roast and wool Sheep Shear for wool, with extra wool from well-bred sheep. Mutton roast and wool Chicken Lays 1 egg an hour. Sheds feathers now and then. Chicken roast and feathers Pig With 3 stars or more of genetics, now and then sheds Enchanted Dust. Pork roast, sometimes Enchanted Dust Horse, donkey, mule, camel Nothing A roast of that animal and leather Llama Nothing Llama roast and feathers Only grown, happy animals lay eggs or shed. Wild cows and goats cannot be milked. A recently sheared sheep or goat drops no wool when killed. Carve roasts at a Meat Hook (see Cooking).

Breeding raises what an animal can give. Care decides how much of it you get. Genetics sets an animal's potential, and care affects how much of it you get. Well-bred animals kept fed and clean give more meat and better food. Genetics Star tier 0 to 199 1 star 200 to 399 2 stars 400 to 599 3 stars 600 to 799 4 stars 800 to 1,000 5 stars Better genetics raise food quality, and high care makes that quality more consistent. Keep animals fed and clean to get the best food from them. Raw genetics also unlocks rarer material drops at 3, 4 and 5 stars.

Right-click your animal with a Co-Ownership Token to link the token to it, then right-click another player with the token, or give it to them and let them right-click with it. Every owner can feed, clean, ride and breed the animal, and it counts towards each owner's limit. To rename an animal, use another named Ownership Token on it. The inspect menu also has a button to give up your ownership.

All the tools are made at the Animal Station. Item Cost Used for Ownership Token 1 iron nugget Claiming or renaming an animal. Used up. Co-Ownership Token 1 iron nugget Sharing an animal with another player. Used up. Glove 2 Leather Cleaning a dirty animal. Not used up. Neutering Tool 2 iron ingots Stopping an animal from breeding. Used up. Trough 1 oak plank Making Universal Feed. To make Universal Feed, place a Trough and right-click it with wheat or vegetables, 4 at a time, until all 4 spots are filled. Rotten food is refused. Then right-click the Trough with an empty hand to take 1 Universal Feed.
An Arcane Trace Detector leads you to an Arcane Cache buried somewhere far away. Each character has their own cache, and nobody else can see or open it. Updated 23 Oct 2026

Everything is made at the Engineer Station, and anyone can craft it. The station makes an Unpowered Trace Detector. Combine it with one Arcane Fuel to power it up. One fuel is good for one cache, and a single craft makes 16 fuel. Unpowered Trace Detector Engineer Station Crafting time: 5 seconds Arcane Crystal 2 Iron Block 2 → Unpowered Trace Detector Arcane Fuel Engineer Station Crafting time: 5 seconds Arcane Crystal Copper Block 4 → Arcane Fuel 16 Yields 16 fuel per craft. Arcane Trace Detector Engineer Station Crafting time: 5 seconds Unpowered Trace Detector Arcane Fuel → Arcane Trace Detector The same recipe recharges a dead detector: no need to re-craft the base item.

Hold a powered detector in either hand while playing a character in the main world. The first time you do, your cache is buried somewhere far from where you stand. It stays there, even over restarts, until you dig it up. Rings of particles appear around you, the detector clicks, and an Arcane Signal bar shows at the top of the screen. Only you can see and hear them. Walk and watch the signal. The closer you get, the more rings you see, the more their colour turns from dark purple to bright purple and then white, the faster the clicks and the fuller the bar. When you are nearly there, the bar is renamed Arcane Signal - dig close by and starts again from empty, and the clicks drop back to slow. From there both build up again as you close in, until the clicks become a steady stream right on top of the cache. The rings and colour only measure distance across the ground, while the clicks and the bar also count how deep the cache is. Dig down. Once you are close, a chest only you can see appears. Click it to open the Arcane Cache. Take your reward. Anything you leave in the cache goes into your inventory when you close it, or drops at your feet if your inventory is full. Chat says You found the arcane source! Your detector is spent. and the detector turns back into an Unpowered Trace Detector, ready for another fuel. Your next cache is buried the next time you hold a powered detector.

You can open one cache every 23 hours 30 minutes. The limit is per player, so switching characters doesn't give you another. If you reach a cache too early, it tells you how long to wait, and both the cache and your powered detector stay as they are. If the cache lies under protected land you can't dig, chat says This ground is warded and the cache moves somewhere else. If you wander very far from your cache, it is buried again closer to you. Events During some events, staff switch the detectors to a single shared cache that everyone hunts at once.
Find an unclaimed ruin, confirm it from soil samples, establish a field camp, excavate by sound, and preserve each find for study or display. Updated 27 Sept 2026

A find is a shape inside the dirt, not a loot block. Expose the shape carefully. When every remaining cube has air on at least one face, those cubes begin dripping. Hold right-click with the brush while aiming at a dripping cube. Looking away pauses that cube; looking back continues it. Keep brushing until one recovered item comes free. A pick never drops the item, and a completely destroyed find drops nothing. The item label tells you whether it is intact, worn, crumbling, or somewhere between. Its starting condition was decided in the ground; careful excavation can preserve it, but cannot turn a naturally damaged piece into a pristine one.

After confirmation, hold the establishment kit and aim at a neighboring chunk rather than the ruin itself. Turn until the camp ghost sits cleanly, then confirm. You become the director, and the tracker will no longer pulse for this ruin. The tents sit beside the dig; the prism marks the ruin ground and the layers below it. Establishing camp does not spend the work day. Use the camp board to read the dossier, manage who may work, review the finds list, and choose Show limits. The glowing cut boundary appears only to you and only briefly. If you have reached your camp limit, close an old camp before claiming another.

Inside the dig site, hold left-click with an excavation tool. The block does not crack like ordinary mining. Listen to the cue, then release the button. Cue Meaning Soft clings, then a louder ready chime Empty fill. Release on the ready chime to lift cubes. Release too soon Nothing leaves. The next hold starts clean. Release too late More cubes leave, giving you less control. The HUD names the stratum and may show how many cuts remain today. Light tools make narrow shafts; heavier tools take wider bites, and a late release always removes more than a timely one. Empty fill can reveal traces of material still touching the hole, which tells you when to slow down. A buried find can be destroyed A find cling means you are cutting into a piece. Punching through it damages the find, and a destroyed cell is gone for good. An ordinary pick can wreck a buried find too, even before anyone establishes a camp.

Make the Archeology Table at a Crafting Table. This workshop is where you make all archaeology tools, including the tracker, prospecting kit, establishment kit, excavation tools, brush, field pencil, and cabinet. Hold the tracker and follow its pulses. They get faster as you approach a ruin that nobody has claimed. If the beeps fade, turn back and try another direction. The tracker stays quiet for a ruin where you already planted a camp. When you are close enough, chat tells you to prospect the ground.

Once every find has been recovered or destroyed, the excavation is exhausted. Close the camp from the board to leave the site and free room for another ruin. You receive a field book; right-click it later to reopen the excavation dossier and finds record even after the tents are gone.

Build any room you like. Shift-right-click a recovered find on a frame, lectern, shelf, armor stand, or a case that accepts plaques to open the same reading available from the camp board. Clicking without Shift keeps the ordinary Minecraft action, such as hanging, rotating, or taking an item.

Use the prospecting kit on shovel-dug earth: dirt, grass, sand, gravel, clay, or mud. Stone and furniture do not count. Hold still while taking each sample; walking away cancels it. Spread samples out and follow the traces until chat confirms the site. Confirmation alone does not claim the ruin.

Take the recovered piece to the cabinet and right-click while holding it. Sneak if you only want the block's ordinary Minecraft use. A dirty piece opens the lab, where each stain names the tool that removes it. A cleaned piece without a drawing can be registered, and an already filed piece opens its reading. To make the drawing, click a field sheet onto the pencil in your inventory, or hold the sheet and use the pencil in your other hand. Sign the sketch, then return to the cabinet and register it with the find in hand.
The Armour Shop changes how your armour, weapons and tools look. A skin changes only the look: the item keeps its stats. Updated 23 Oct 2026

Open the shop anywhere with /armourshop. Run /armourshop and choose Armour or Items, then a category. Armour skins are shown piece by piece: helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots. Each skin's tooltip shows the Skin Scroll it costs and the kind of item it fits, such as medium steel armour or swords. Click a piece. The shop skins the first item in your inventory that fits, whether you carry it or wear it, and uses up one scroll of that exact tier. A full armour set takes four clicks and four scrolls. If you don't have the right scroll, or nothing you carry fits, nothing is used up. Armour you forged in Advanced Crafting only takes skins made for its metal. Forged weapons take any skin of their type. To undo an armour skin, use the free Reset to Default category. It has a plain look for leather and for every metal in light, medium, heavy, infantry and mage armour.
Command Aliases What it does Notes /armourshop None Opens the skin shop. None

Ranked players can design their own skins on the website. Get a code with /token create skin, or start a new skin from the Skins tab of your website profile. How often you can do this depends on your rank. Upload your textures and name the skin. You can choose to rename the item to the skin's name. Once staff approve it, it appears after the next daily update in the shop's Player Armor or Player Items category. Only you can see it, and applying it costs no scroll. Rank What you can upload Noble Weapons, tools, bows, crossbows and books Gilded Everything above, plus armour sets Ascended Everything above, plus 3D items, 3D helmets, shields, guns and masks Legacy Everything Ascended can

Each skin costs one scroll of a set tier. Some skins are free. Common Item Skin Scroll Rare Item Skin Scroll Epic Item Skin Scroll Legendary Item Skin Scroll Common Item Skin Scroll You earn scrolls from the higher weekly activity rewards, from the daily reward ranked players get for revealing all their daily tasks, and from Trial Room loot. A higher tier never stands in for a lower one.
Write a letter, seal it, and hand it over yourself or send it by bird to any character on the server. Updated 22 Oct 2026

The flight takes a quarter of a second per block between you and the recipient: where they are if they are playing that character, otherwise where the character was last. Shortest flight 30 seconds Longest flight 10 minutesfor about 2,400 blocks or more Cost Free When the bird arrives, the recipient gets the letter at once if they are playing that character, alive, and have a free inventory space. Otherwise it waits, for as long as it takes, and arrives as soon as all three are true. If they are offline or playing another character, you are told it is waiting. If the recipient's character dies first, waiting letters go to its heir (see wills), or back to you if it has none. A recipient with a linked Discord account also gets a Discord message when a bird arrives. It does not say who sent the letter or what it says.

Letter Crafting Table Requires: None Paper Paper Paper Paper → Letter Write in the Letter and sign it to seal it. Craft a Letter from four Paper in a square and write in it like a book. Signing it seals it: the title becomes the letter's name, and the author is not shown. You need to be playing a character to sign or edit a letter. The seal breaks the first time someone opens the letter to read it, and it becomes an Opened Letter. Putting it on a lectern or a chiselled bookshelf, or clicking a door or barrel while holding it, leaves the seal intact.

Right-click a bird mailbox without sneaking. Put one Letter in the slot. It can be blank, sealed or opened, but nothing else can travel with it. Pick the recipient from the list of character heads. It shows every living character listed for mail, online or offline, except your own. Click Confirm. The letter leaves your inventory and a bird flies off with it. Loading 3D preview… Bird Mailbox Place it on the floor; it stands 2 blocks tall. Sneak to break it. If you close the list without confirming, you get the letter back. The bird cannot fly between worlds, so a character in another world is refused at Confirm and the letter stays with you. To keep the character you are playing off the list, run /rpcharacter mail off.
Brew drinks in a cauldron, then distil and age them when the recipe calls for it. Donators can also design their own drink on the website. Updated 22 Oct 2026

Command Aliases What it does Notes /brew help [page] /brewery help, /breweryx help Shows the paged command list. Available to every player. /brew info /brewery info, /breweryx info Shows your current drunkenness percentage and quality. None

Noble rank and above can add their own drink recipe to the server. Link your Discord account and join the server once so your rank is known. Then open the Drinks tab on your profile and choose New drink, or run /token create drink in game for a code. Fill in the recipe: ingredients from a fixed list, cooking time, distilling, barrel wood and age, difficulty and alcohol. Then the look: name, lore, potion effects, a shimmer, and either a colour or a bottle texture. Higher ranks can also add a drink message, a line shown to whoever drinks it. Submit it. Staff review every drink, and you hear back on Discord. Once approved, the recipe is on the server within a few minutes. A custom bottle texture can take up to a day and needs the updated resource pack. You don't get a bottle. Your drink becomes a normal recipe that anyone can brew if they know the ingredients. Some potion effects are not allowed, such as speed, strength, regeneration and invisibility. Rank New drink every Name colours Bottle texture Drink message Noble 28 days 1 No No Gilded 21 days 2 Yes No Ascended 14 days Up to 8 Yes Yes Legacy 7 days Up to 8 Yes Yes The wait is shared with custom skins and starts when you take the code. A code you never use, or a drink staff deny, does not count once the code expires.

Every brew shows its quality as 1 to 5 stars. Alcoholic drinks are marked Alcoholic, but their exact strength stays hidden. Each drink tells you how drunk you are, and /brew info shows it again. Bread and milk sober you up a little. Log off very drunk and you may come back with a hangover. A Brew Sealing Table is crafted from 2 glass bottles over 4 planks and looks like a smoker. Sealing a brew hides how it was made, so it looks like a finished product when you sell it.

Ferment. Place a cauldron over fire, soul fire, lava, a magma block or a lit campfire and fill it with water. Right-click it with each ingredient. Right-click with a clock to see how long it has been boiling. Bottle. Right-click the cauldron with a glass bottle to fill one bottle. Distil, if the recipe needs it. Put the bottles in a brewing stand with glowstone dust. It keeps distilling for as many runs as the recipe allows. Age, if the recipe needs it. Leave the bottles in a barrel. One barrel year is 20 real minutes. A normal Minecraft barrel holds up to 6 brews. You can also build a larger wooden barrel; its sign must include the word "barrel". Small built barrels hold 1 row of items and large ones 3 rows. The type of wood matters for some recipes.
Set up a card table almost anywhere and play for real denars: Blackjack, Tenceur Hold'em, Five-Draw, or Free play with no rules at all. Updated 23 Oct 2026

Blackjack tables are run by guilds. Only a guild leader can place one, and the guild needs a free table from its Auto Dealer Tables upgrade (see guilds). The house plays with the guild bank's money: if the bank can't cover the bets, the round is called off and everyone gets their bet back. Right-click your box on the felt with coins to bet, and again to add more. The first bet gives everyone else 10 seconds to join in. Bets below the table minimum are given back. On your turn, right-click the shoe for a card, or say hit, stand, double or split. The usual blackjack rules apply, and /games help has the details. Walk away once the round has started and you lose your bet. Between rounds, a guild member can stand at the dealer's spot and right-click the shoe to deal by hand. The dealer sets the limits and opens and closes betting with the /games bet commands below.

Command What it does /games help Opens the rule books: one for each game, plus an index. /games bet <hit|stand|double|split> Your Blackjack move. Typing the word in chat on your turn does the same. /games bet <check|call|raise|fold|allin> Your poker move. Typing the word in chat on your turn does the same. /games bet <min|max> <amount> Sets the Blackjack table's smallest or largest bet, as its dealer between rounds. /games bet <open|close> Opens or closes betting, as the Blackjack dealer. /games poker configure <buy-in> <chips> <rebuys> <ante> <minutes> Turns your empty Hold'em table into a tournament. A buy-in of 0 makes it a cash table again. /games poker <buyin|rebuy> Buys into a tournament before it starts, or back in between hands when you are out of chips. /games poker bet <chips> Puts tournament chips out on your turn. /games poker <start|finish|status> The host starts play or pays out the prize at the end. Anyone can check the status. /games poker kick <player> The host removes a player between hands. After play starts, they lose their buy-in. /wager <denars> Offers the stack you are holding as a stake, valued at that many denars per item. /wager <accept|decline> Votes on another player's offered stake.

Five-Draw seats and bets like Hold'em, but with no blinds. Everyone gets five hidden cards. On your draw turn, right-click the cards you want to swap, then right-click the shoe to get that many new ones. To keep all five, say draw instead. Then there is one more round of betting.

No turns, no dealer, no rules. Right-click the shoe with an empty hand to take a card, and click cards then the shoe to throw them away. Right-click the felt with coins to add them to the middle. If you walk away, your coins come back to you. Warning The table's owner can take the whole middle at any time by sneaking and right-clicking the shoe. Only play at a table whose owner you trust.

Right-click the felt with coins to sit down. Once two players are seated, any of them can right-click the shoe to deal. The blinds are taken from you automatically at the start of a hand. If you can't cover yours, you are all in. On your turn, put your coins on the felt first, then say check, call, raise or fold. The table only counts coins you actually put out. allin puts in every coin you carry, and you can only call for less than the bet once you have no coins left. Walk away mid-hand and you only get back what nobody has matched yet this round. After folding, you get nothing back. The table's owner can turn an empty table into a tournament with a buy-in, starting chips, rebuys, an ante and a time after which the blinds double. Players play with chips, the buy-ins make up the prize, and leaving after play starts forfeits your entry. See the /games poker commands below.

Your cards float in front of you. Only you see their faces. Left-click one to look closer, and press your swap-hands key (F) to show your whole hand to the table. The deck on the table is the shoe: right-click it to draw, deal or take your turn. Bets are made with gold coins in your inventory, not your pouch or bank. Withdraw some first with /deco toitem (see Denar Economy). Right-click the felt holding coins: each click puts one coin item down at its full value, so a Pouch of Gold Denars is 100. Silver coins aren't accepted. On your turn, type your move in chat as a single word, like hit or fold. Winnings are paid in coins. Tax is taken from your profit, never from the stake you get back. Walking more than 6 blocks away takes you out of the game. What you get back depends on the game, as described below. /games help opens a rule book for each game.

Make a Deck of Cards at the Tool Station from 2 Paper. Hold it and right-click the top of a solid block (slabs work), but not one that already has a table. You need to be playing a character. Pick a game. Hold'em first asks for the blinds and how often to shuffle. Five-Draw and Free play are set up straight away. Blackjack tables belong to guilds (see Blackjack). The table belongs to the character who placed it, and passes to their heir if they die. Money left on it is not inherited. As the owner, sneak and right-click the deck between rounds to change a Hold'em or Blackjack table's settings, or punch the deck to pick the table up again and get your Deck of Cards back.

At Hold'em, Five-Draw and Free play cash tables, once you have coins on the table, you can also stake an item. Hold it and type /wager with what each item is worth in denars: the whole stack you hold is offered. The other seated players have 30 seconds to vote with /wager accept or /wager decline, and more than half must agree. If nobody else is seated, it counts straight away. Then you have 10 seconds to click the felt with the item.

Everything you do on the server, you do as a character. Your character is the one who speaks in chat, gets injured and can die for good. Updated 22 Oct 2026 Warning Until you pick a character on the selection screen, you cannot chat or use commands. The only ones that work there are /linkdiscord and /rpcharacter menu, which reopens the screen.

Anything you type without a command goes to your default channel, which starts as in-character speech (rp). Change it with /channel <id>, or run /channel alone to see your current one. /channeltoggle <id> hides or shows an out-of-character channel in your own chat. Channel Command Who hears it What it's for In-character speech /rp Within 15 blocks Normal talking as your character Shout /shout Within 24 blocks A raised voice Yell /yell (/y) Within 48 blocks Your loudest shout, in bold red Whisper /whisper (/wh) Within 2 blocks Quiet words for someone right beside you Action /me Within 20 blocks Emotes and actions, shown as narration Scene /scene Within 20 blocks Describing the scene, with no speech bubble Local OOC /looc Within 20 blocks Out-of-character talk with people nearby Global OOC /ooc Everyone online Server-wide out-of-character chat Guild OOC /gooc Your guild Out-of-character talk with your guild Faction OOC /fooc Your faction Out-of-character talk with your faction Realm OOC /rooc Your whole realm Includes your overlord and vassal factions Party OOC /pooc Your RP party Out-of-character talk with your /rpcharacter party Note Walls and distance affect in-character speech. A speaker who is partly blocked or near the edge of range comes through with cut-off words. If you can barely hear them, their name shows as ???, and at the very edge you only get *muffled voices*. Glass and leaves block very little sound, obsidian a lot.

The clues you write during creation describe your character: visual features, smells, home, habits and so on. Every character also has an automatic clue that gives away their race. Low-effort or false clues can be punished. /rpcharacter clues shows your own list. When a clue is left at a scene, characters within a few blocks of it can notice it over time, and Wisdom and Intelligence improve the odds. Clues fade: an old clue is harder to read than a fresh one, and each disappears within two days.

One message every 3 seconds. /rooc <message> Out-of-character chat with your whole realm, overlord and vassals included. One message every 3 seconds. /pooc <message> Out-of-character chat with your RP party. One message every 3 seconds.

The creator takes a while, so set aside some time. On the selection screen, choose New character, then Create character. You need a free slot for a living character. The creator is a series of screens with Next and Back buttons: Answer whether you are 18 or older in real life. This decides whether you can join age-restricted roleplay. Name your character. Choose a class and a race. Set your character's age. Pick background traits: homeland, cataclysm, reclamation, motivation, gift, virtue, combat, physical and celestial. Spend 12 attribute points. Pick personality traits. A callous, cynical, deceitful, greedy or spiteful personality can also take up to two evil archetypes, once your account is at least 24 hours old. Optionally add backstory injuries (as many as you like) and one prosthetic. Arcane prosthetics need fuel to stay powered. Write a description of 32 to 256 characters: how your character looks, sounds and comes across. Write your clues: at least 2, or 4 for an evil character, each 12 to 48 characters long (see Clues). Review everything, change anything you want, and confirm. If you close the creator partway, /rpcharacter menu reopens it. You can also create characters on the website with the same steps: run /token create profile in game, sign in on your profile and choose New character. Skins are optional. Upload them on the website under your character's Wardrobe, then swap between them in game with /rpcharacter wardrobe. After creation, /rpcharacter edit reopens your choices. Some of them lock after a while, and the editor shows how long each one has left. Once you are playing, /rpcharacter kit starter gives you an iron hunting knife, 32 gold coins, 32 dry rations, a writable book, a bundle and a brown bed. Each character can claim it once, and you must wait 48 hours between claims on different characters.

In most deaths, your belongings go into a grave chest at the spot where you died. A hologram above it shows who killed you and how long the grave has left. Right-click it to take your things back. Only you can open it, unless you run /grave unlock to let anyone loot your newest grave, but thieves can still try to rob it (see Thievery). After 40 minutes the grave disappears and drops whatever is left on the ground. When another player kills you, the money in your pouch also drops as coins where you died (see Denar Economy). Carry a Grave Insurance ticket when you die and it binds to your grave. Right-click the ticket from anywhere to get your items back. The ticket is used up, and it cannot open a grave that only your killer can open.

A healing injury goes away after 72 hours, counted in real time even while you are offline, and its attribute penalties ease as it heals. A physician can also treat it with surgery. If it turns permanent, it stays for good. With a broken or lost arm you drop whatever is in your off hand and any two-handed item you hold. A prosthetic can replace a lost arm or leg, but nothing replaces lost sight. Healing injury Effects at first Permanent form Permanent effects Broken Arm −4 Strength, −2 Constitution, Weakness, no off hand or two-handed items One-Handed −3 Strength, −1 Constitution, Weakness, no off hand or two-handed items Broken Leg −4 Dexterity, Slowness One-Legged −3 Dexterity, Slowness Half Blind −1 Dexterity Blind −4 Dexterity, −2 Wisdom, Blindness To roleplay an injury with someone's agreement, run /rpcharacter injure <player> within 10 blocks of them and pick the injury from a menu. They have 30 seconds to accept it.

Some regions are permadeath zones, and a title tells you when you enter one. Dying there can kill your character for good: the chance is 10% for each injury your character already has. If your character survives, the death costs an injury instead. A healing injury you already have turns permanent, or, if you have none, you gain a new healing injury. Deaths while you fight in a started war battle (see Factions) never kill your character, injure it or give strikes. Fights between players start out nonlethal. /pvp start warns everyone within 80 blocks that a fight begins in 10 seconds, and the fight lasts 15 minutes or until the player who started it runs /pvp end. In a started fight, losing can give your character a strike: A nonlethal winner knocks you out. You stay down for up to 5 minutes while they choose to spare you or give you a strike. You can still talk, but you cannot fight or use items. If they do not choose, you are spared. A lethal winner (/pvp lethal, then confirm) gives you a strike as soon as they kill you. You wake at your spawn point with your items, though not the money in your pouch. If they are able to loot graves, your items go into a grave instead. Your first strike is a healing injury and the second a permanent one. The third kills your character, and only the killer can open its grave. When a strike would kill you, a nonlethal winner can wound or maim you instead. The same player must wait 24 hours before striking you again. Kills outside a started fight, and deaths with no player to blame, give no strike. During an evil RP session, any strike kills your character. Check your strikes with /rpcharacter strikes. For practice, /duel <player> challenges someone within 16 blocks to a duel of up to 10 minutes. Nobody dies or loses anything in a duel.

Sneak and right-click another player with an empty hand to see their character card: name, gender, age, birthday, race and description. /rpcharacter profile <player> shows the same card. A player wearing a mask hides their identity: in-character chat shows them as Masked, and their card cannot be read. /tfmc masks gives you one (see Roleplay Tools).

While playing, you can change your character's alias (a name others see in place of theirs), gender, description, birthday and name colour with the /rpcharacter commands listed below. Players with Noble, Gilded, Ascended or Legacy rank can also use colour codes in chat and in their description.

Rank Switch cooldown Living characters Name colours Wardrobe slots Commoner 7 days 3 0 1 Noble 5 days 3 1 1 Gilded 4 days 4 2 2 Ascended 3 days 5 20 3 Legacy 2 days 5 20 3 Name colours is how many colours your character's name can blend into a gradient. With 0, your name stays white.

/roll rolls from 1 to 200. /roll <max> rolls from 1 to your own maximum, and you can add a modifier such as /roll 20 +3. /roll <attribute> rolls a d20 plus that attribute's modifier, from −5 at 0 or 1 points to +5 at 20 points (10 or 11 points give +0). You and everyone within 20 blocks see the result.

Each time you join, you arrive at the character selection screen. It shows your living characters one at a time: use the arrows to look through them, then click Play to enter the world where that character left off. Each character keeps its own inventory, ender chest, position, health and experience. Profession levels are shared between them (see Professions). You must link your Discord account before you can play (see Getting Started). The same screen lets you create a New character, read a character's background and clues, and visit Memorials for characters who have died or gone missing. End character kills a character for good and cannot be undone. To get back to the selection screen while playing, run /rpcharacter menu and stand still for 5 seconds. This does not work while you are dead, falling, riding, duelling or in a fight. Switching to a different character has a cooldown that depends on your rank. It counts from the last time you switched, and it also applies to creating a new character while you have a living one. You can always go back to the character you were last playing. During an evil RP session you cannot switch at all.

/will names one living character as your character's heir. Your own characters count, and nobody is told. The will is fixed when your character dies for good, and 24 hours later the heir receives everything except your guild's locks, which go to the guild's leader, or to the realm's leader if the guild has none. The heir collects stored items with /estate collect. With no living heir, money goes to your guild and property to its leader; with no guild, the estate waits 7 days and is then held by staff. Leading a guild or realm never passes by will. You can also change your will on your website profile.
Your class decides what equipment you can use and which skills you get. Professions are levelled separately, through gathering and crafting. Updated 22 Oct 2026

The current story act sets the highest level a path, Mage or Musketeer can reach. The server is in Act 1, so the cap is 11. Base classes stop at level 6 whatever the act, which is another reason to pick your path at level 2. Class EXP comes from killing creatures and from Codex discoveries. Act Level cap Prologue 6 Act 1 (current) 11 Act 2 16 Act 3 21

Your starting attributes are set while creating your character. An Attribute Tome gives you more points to spend in /attributes. Each attribute takes up to 20 points. Attribute Each point gives Strength +1 Physical Damage Dexterity +1 Projectile Damage Constitution +0.3 Max Health Intelligence +1 Max Mana, +0.01 Mana Regeneration Wisdom +0.75 Cooldown Reduction Charisma +1 Recoil Reduction, +1 Reload Reduction, +1 Magic Damage, +0.25 Critical Strike Chance

Every path is one of three types. Martial paths have only passive skills, semi-casters mix spells and passives, and full casters have only spells. Spells cost mana and are cast from your skill bar; the magic schools listed are the ones their spells draw on. Archer Deadly marksmen who deal steady damage from a distance and are good at keeping a safe position. Path Type Equipment Ranger Martial Longbows, Light Armour Trapper Semi-caster Crossbows, Light Armour Arcane Archer Full caster Shortbows, Light Armour Bard Charismatic musicians who channel mana through music to bless allies and slow enemies down. Path Type Equipment Minstrel Semi-caster Lutes, Light Armour Virtuoso Full caster Lutes, Light Armour Siren Full caster Lutes, Light Armour Guardian Unyielding defenders who draw attention, absorb damage and push enemies around the battlefield. Path Type Equipment Juggernaut Martial Warhammers, Battleaxes, Greataxes, Greathammers, Shields, Heavy Armour Warden Semi-caster Spears, Swords, Polearms, Shields, Battle Standards, Heavy Armour Runeward Full caster Swords, Daggers, Spears, Shields, Heavy Armour Paladin Resolute soldiers who strengthen themselves and protect others, as duellists or as support. Path Type Equipment Crusader Martial Warhammers, Greathammers, Longswords, Shields, Battle Standards, Medium Armour Templar Semi-caster Swords, Warhammers, Spears, Polearms, Shields, Medium Armour Cleric Full caster Warhammers, Swords, Spears, Shields, Light Armour Warrior Mobile fighters who mix attacks and flexible skills to deal heavy damage at the front. Path Type Equipment Berserker Martial Greataxes, Battleaxes, Greathammers, Shortswords, Medium Armour Warlord Martial Longswords, Swords, Spears, Polearms, Battleaxes, Battle Standards, Medium Armour Spellblade Semi-caster Swords, Longswords, Shortswords, Daggers, Medium Armour Mage The hardest class. Mages build their own weapons from parts, cast spells from runes and are very expensive to gear. Equipment: Mage Staffs, Mage Wands, Mage Blades, Mage Armour. Musketeer Experts in guns and gadgets. They have no skills, but build firearms to order, many of which pierce armour. Equipment: Pistols, Rifles, Shotguns, Rocket Launchers, Infantry Armour. Mage spells come from runes set into weapons you build yourself (see Magic). Only Musketeers can fire guns (see Guns & Gunsmithing). Note Some gear made before the paths were added still lists the old base classes, so no path can use it.

Professions are shared by all your characters: each one plays at the highest level any of them has reached. Profession points arrive unspent on every character, and the upgrades you buy in /profession stay with the character that bought them. Profession How to level it Crafter Smelt stone, metals, glass and other materials; mine ores and stone; repair tools. Forager Kill farm animals and harvest crops that you grow. Herborist Gather Nether fungi and chop logs, wood and mangrove roots. Open /skills, shift-left-click a skill, then left-click a slot to bind it. Right-click a slot to empty it. To cast a bound spell, press F (swap hands), then the number shown on the action bar. Each slot only takes certain kinds of skill, and new slots open as your path levels up: Type Slot I Level 7 Level 12 Level 17 Martial Passive Slot III: passive, 25% weaker with a 25% longer cooldown Slot II: passive None Semi-caster Spell or passive Slot III: passive Slot II: spell or passive None Full caster Spell Slot II: spell Slot III: spell Slot IV: spell Skills unlock at class level 2 and can be upgraded to skill level 4. Paths get 2 skill points at levels 7, 12 and 17, and each upgrade costs 1 point. Picking a path above those levels still gives you their slots and points. A Skill Retraining Manual refunds the points you have spent. Foe Sense and Duel Instinct are always on and need no slot.

You choose one of seven classes while creating your character. Archer, Bard, Guardian, Paladin and Warrior are starting points: they have no skills and no class equipment of their own. At class level 2 each of them splits into three paths (subclasses), and the path you pick decides your gear and skills. The game reminds you to pick one with /class, and your level carries over. Mage and Musketeer have no paths and keep their own equipment from the start. /class opens Class Selection and /subclass shows the paths of your current class. Click a class once to select it and again to confirm. You can only pick paths of your current class, and changing your base class removes your path, so the menu asks first. Your first class and your first path are free. Any change is also free for the first 5 days after the character was created. After that, changes cost 100, then 1,000, then 3,000 denars, and 3,000 for every change after that. The menu shows what your next change costs. You pay from your pouch or from the bank, and the full price must come from one of them.
The Codex is your character's journal of discoveries. Type /codex while playing a character to open it. Updated 23 Oct 2026

Category How entries unlock Points of Interest Travel to notable places around the world. Research Right-click a Completed Thesis from Research. Important Figures Right-click a Completed Thesis about a historical figure. Special Discoveries The world's deepest secrets. Achievements Milestones, such as your first death or how much of the Codex you have found, plus a few surprises.

Most discoveries belong to your whole account. When another of your characters starts playing, it receives your discoveries and their experience. Research entries and a few achievements are the exception: they stay with the character who earned them. Your other characters can still read an entry they did not find themselves, and the entry shows which of your characters knows it in character. Play the others as if they don't.
Command Aliases What it does /codex None Opens your discovery journal.

The first page shows each category and how much of it you have unlocked. Inside a category, locked entries are hidden. An unlocked entry shows its name and description, and some also show the date you found it and the percentage of players who have unlocked it. Some entries, such as research and important figures, can be clicked to read more. Every new entry gives you experience, and chat tells you how much.

A companion is a little personality to share your adventures with. Give it a name, look after it, play together and teach it tricks. The more time you spend together, the stronger your bond becomes. Updated 11 Oct 2026

A happy companion needs food, attention, rest and a little grooming. Watch how your pet behaves and check its care sheet when something seems wrong. Hunger, mood, energy, cleanliness and health all matter. Petting it with an empty hand lets you check in: it may show that it is hungry, tired, dirty or feeling unwell. Food helps with hunger, play and affection lift its spirits, and sleep gives it energy for another outing. Care supplies for every companion, including frogs What you want to do Item you need How to use it Feed your pet Meat Meal or Fish Meal Right-click your pet to give it food. Clean and groom it Pet Brush Right-click to groom your pet. You keep the brush. Treat a sick pet Pet Medicine A Physician crafts it at the Medicine Station. Right-click a sick or weakened pet to give it medicine. Train and reward it Fish Snack or Biscuit Treat Hold a treat to begin training, then give treats as rewards. Play fetch Pet Ball, Bone Plush, Tug Rope, Mouse Plush or Teddy Bear Plush Craft a toy at the Animal Station and throw it for your pet to fetch. Make a shelter Pet House Craft it at the Animal Station, place it on the ground and right-click to open your shelter. Give affection Empty hand Right-click your pet to check on it and give it attention. Get food, grooming supplies, treats and toys at the Animal Station. For a sick companion, get Pet Medicine, crafted by a Physician at the Medicine Station. These supplies work for all companions.Meat Meal and Fish Meal are their meals; Fish Snack and Biscuit Treat are training rewards. Food, medicine and rewarded treats are used up. Keep your pet fed and rested before asking it to practise or play, and avoid feeding it more when it is already full. A neglected pet can become ill and too weak to stand. Medicine helps it recover, but it still needs food, rest and care. Other players can help feed, groom and heal your companion too.

Choose a companion you would like to spend time with. You can have dogs, cats, foxes and even a frog. Each pet has its own personality: some are friendly and eager to play, while others are shy or protective of their space. They keep their name, preferences and learned tricks as you spend time together. Craft companion eggs at the Animal Station. Some require the Pet Master perk in the Forager profession; ten companions require a donator rank instead. Their recipes appear in the station once you meet the requirement below. Right-click with an egg and follow the naming prompts in chat to welcome your new pet. Once it is beside you, sneak-right-click it with an empty hand to open its care sheet. This is where you can see how it feels, its personality and your growing bond. They hatch from Wolf Spawn Eggs and Cat Spawn Eggs, whose separate Animal Station recipes use the Breeder I perk. Each companion has its own egg. Craft eggs, food, grooming supplies, treats and toys at the Animal Station to prepare for your adventures together.

Choose a Pet Ball, Bone Plush, Tug Rope, Mouse Plush or Teddy Bear Plush at the Animal Station and throw it for your pet to fetch. It chases the toy and brings it back to you. Play cheers it up, but a tired or sick companion needs a rest first.

A place to keep your companions between adventures. Craft a Pet House at the Animal Station, place it on the ground and right-click it to browse your companions. Only you can open your house. Moving or breaking it leaves your stored companions safe: place a house again whenever you want to visit them. Loading Pet House… Sheltered pets keep their needs as they are, ready for your next visit. Their needs also pause while you are offline. When you are playing, companions left outside still need looking after, so make the shelter part of your routine. Warning Keep your companion away from danger: a pet that dies is lost. Releasing a pet through Release forever also means saying goodbye permanently.

Learning takes patience, encouragement and treats. Your companion already knows how to follow you. You can teach it more, from sitting and staying in place to jumping, offering a paw or lying down to rest. Frogs have their own gestures, including sticking out their tongue and croaking. Open the pet's Tricks menu to see what it can learn and how it is progressing. When your pet is healthy, fed and rested, hold a Fish Snack or Biscuit Treat and right-click it to begin a training session. Choose a word or short phrase in chat, then pick the trick you want it to mean. Practise together and give a treat promptly after each attempt. Early efforts can be clumsy; encouragement helps, and rewarded successes teach it more quickly. Keep sessions relaxed and give your pet a break when it stops listening. Once it has learned a trick, you can ask for it using the word you taught, without needing a treat every time. Look at your pet as you speak, or include its name, such as Toby sit, to address it nearby. Coming over to you and following you are different tricks: one calls it close, while the other asks it to accompany you.
You cook on furniture placed in the world, not in a menu. Food keeps track of how fresh it is, how it was cooked and how it was seasoned, and has a quality from 1 to 5 stars. Updated 23 Oct 2026

All cooking furniture and tools are made at the Meal Prep Station from iron, stone or oak planks (see Furniture). Right-click a piece with an ingredient to put it in. Right-click with an empty hand to take it back out, or to work the station: churn, stir, turn the spit. To cut or carve, hit the Cutting Board or Meat Hook while holding a Cutting Knife. The Frying Pan, Saucepan, Pot and Oven Top only cook when they sit directly on a lit Oven Bottom. Right-click the Oven Bottom with logs (up to 6), then with Flint and Steel to light it. The Fire Pit goes on a lit campfire instead.

Each hit with the Cutting Knife on the Meat Hook takes off one piece, in this order. Hanging on the hook Yields in order Whole chicken 2 chicken legs, 3 chicken, then 2 bones Other roasts 7 pieces of that meat, then 4 bones Sausage chain 5 sausages How many pieces a roast actually holds depends on how well the animal was bred and cared for (see Animal Husbandry).

Recipe Input Output Cut vegetables 2 raw carrots, potatoes, beetroots, pumpkins, tomatoes, onions, lettuce, cucumbers or corn 1 cut vegetable Chop vegetables 1 cut vegetable 1 chopped vegetable Chop 1 olive, pistachio, rhubarb or garlic 1 chopped garnish Cut seafood 1 whole fish, jellyfish or octopus 1 fish fillet, jellyfish cubes or octopus pieces

Each character has its own hunger, and a full stomach does not heal you the way it does in normal Minecraft. As you eat, your diet is rated from Terrible to Fantastic. A better diet gives you more damage, health, mana and critical chance, and shorter cooldowns. Eating the same few ingredients over and over lowers your rating, so vary your meals.

A carrot and potato soup to learn the basics. You need 2 carrots, 2 potatoes, a Water Bucket, a few logs, Flint and Steel, a Cutting Board, Cutting Knife, Oven Bottom, Pot, Masher, Ladle and Bowl. Put the 2 carrots on the Cutting Board and hit it with the Cutting Knife. You get 1 cut carrot. Do the same with the potatoes. Place the Oven Bottom and put the Pot on top. Fill the pot with the Water Bucket. Add logs to the Oven Bottom and light them with Flint and Steel. When the water boils, add the cut carrot and mash it with the Masher. The pot won't take anything else until you do. Then add the cut potato and mash that too. Right-click the pot with the Ladle to take a serving. One pot gives 3. Place the Bowl, right-click it with the full ladle, then right-click the bowl with an empty hand to eat. Once mashed, a soup takes one salt, one pepper, one garnish and one spice to season it.

Station How to use it Cutting Board Put up to 2 of the same ingredient on it and hit it with the Cutting Knife. See the recipes below. Frying Pan Add Butter first: without it, everything in a hot pan burns within 10 seconds. One Butter lasts 30 seconds. Fries raw meat, sausages, eggs, seafood and cut vegetables. Pot Fill with a Water Bucket. Boils cut vegetables, chicken, red meat, fish fillets, jellyfish and octopus, which you mash into soup. Saucepan Fill with a cup of water or milk, add ingredients, then ladle the sauce onto food on a Plate. Liquid Container Fill with a water or milk bucket, then right-click with an Empty Cup to fill a cup. Fire Pit Place it on a lit campfire and put any roast on the spit. Right-click the handle with an empty hand to turn it. Each turn cooks it a little more, so stop before it burns. Meat Hook Hangs from a ceiling. Hang a roast or sausage chain on it and hit it with the Cutting Knife to carve one piece at a time. Milling Stone Right-click it with 8 or more wheat in hand (it uses 8), then right-click with an empty hand to grind 1 flour. Mixing Bowl Add flour, a cup of water and yeast, in that order. You can also add 1 sugar and up to 2 different fruits. Stir 3 times to make dough. Bread Tray Fill the moulds with dough before putting the tray in the Oven Top over a lit Oven Bottom. Each mould bakes 2 bread. Take it out before it burns. Let the dough rise first: its description shows Unrisen, Rising or Risen. Butter Churn Right-click with a Milk Bucket, then churn 3 times. Add salt or a spice before collecting for salted or spiced butter. Collect the butter while carrying a Butter Plate. Sausage Maker Add 3 pieces of meat, then crank it with paper in your hand (uses 1 sheet). Carve the sausage chain into 5 sausages at a Meat Hook. Empty cauldron Right-click with a soup or sauce to pour it away. You get the empty ladle back.
A node is a guild's mine, farm, forestry or quarry. Your guild stocks it with tools and other fittings, and it keeps producing resources for as long as it stays active. Updated 22 Oct 2026

A node's efficiency, shown in its menu, also sets the cycle length: at 0% a cycle takes four times as long as at 100%. A new node starts at 50%. Efficiency rises by 0.1% per guild member each hour, up to 1% an hour, and is capped at 25% per member, so a guild needs four members to reach 100%. Changing the node type costs 40%.

Upgrades are paid in denars from the guild bank, and each level shortens the cycle and adds faction prestige. Downgrading refunds 80% of that level's cost. The figures below are the cost of reaching each level from the one before. Level 1 Starting level Level 2 40 Level 3 80 Level 4 160 Level 5 320 Level 6 640 Level 7 1,280 Level 8 2,560 Level 9 5,120 Level 10 10,060 An active node also costs upkeep, taken from the guild bank at the start of each new day. Upkeep is 4 denars a day per level, plus extra for the focus and fittings.

Only members of the owning guild can change a node. Transfer Node makes it claimable: the next guild leader who uses it takes it over, if their guild has no node yet. Delete Node cannot be undone. You get the node block back and any output it was holding, but its level and fittings are lost.

Anyone can craft a General Node at a crafting table, but only a member of a guild can set one up. A one-person guild is enough. Each guild can run one node, and each chunk can hold one node. General Node Crafting Table Requires: None Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks Gold Ingot Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks → One General Node can run any of the six node types. Loading 3D preview…

Place the node on the floor and right-click it to open its menu. Pick a node type, then a production focus and fittings such as tools, a refinery, light or irrigation. Put a barrel directly under the node and fill it with what the fittings use. Put a hopper directly above it to collect the output. The node will not start without both. Activate the node. The guild bank must hold at least one day's upkeep. The node takes its fitting materials from the barrel when you activate it and again every 24 hours. If the barrel or hopper is missing at that point, the node shuts off. Output goes into the hopper, and only spills on top of the node once the hopper is full. The node must be inactive before you change its type, focus or fittings, change its level, or delete it. Deactivating refunds the barrel materials taken since the last output, as long as the barrel and hopper are both still there.

Type Production focus Fittings Base cycle Ore Mine Iron Ore Mine, Copper Ore Mine, Rare Ore Mine, Gemstone Mine Tools, Refinery, Light, Explosives 4 hours Magical Mine Dust Mine, Artifact Mine Tools, Refinery, Light, Explosives 4 hours Farm Vegetable Farm, Onion Farm, Exotic Farm, Yeast Production, Fruit Orchard, Exotic Fruit Orchard Hoes, Fertilizer, Irrigation 2 hours Plantation Material Plantation, Spice Plantation, Sweet Spice Plantation Hoes, Fertilizer, Irrigation 2 hours Forestry Log Forestry, Bark Forestry, Rare Wood Forestry Axes, Refinery, Irrigation 1 hour Quarry Stone Quarry, Salt Quarry, Gold Quarry Shovels, Refinery, Light, Explosives 1 hour The focus decides what the node produces. Fittings mostly change how long a cycle takes, and better fittings are faster. Only steel, abyssalite and mythril tools raise the yield, while stone and iron tools sometimes produce nothing. Some choices need another one first: Gemstone and Artifact mines need diamond tools or better, and Rare Wood Forestry needs diamond axes or better. Fruit orchards and spice plantations need basic irrigation or better. Advanced Fertilizer needs steam-powered irrigation.
The server's money is the denar (d). One gold denar is worth 100 silver denars. Each of your characters has its own money, so switching character switches purse. Updated 23 Oct 2026

Each character has two balances. Check both with /deco bal. Your pouch is the money you carry. Coins you pick up and money you earn go here, and you pay from it. Your bank is your savings. You can only move money in or out while standing at the bank of your faction or guild, so you need to belong to one. Use /deco deposit <amount> and /deco withdraw <amount>. Warning If another player kills you, your whole pouch drops as coins where you fell, for anyone to pick up. Your bank is never touched. Other deaths, and deaths in a scheduled battle, don't cost you your pouch.

Coins are real items you can hand over, hide or lose. Pouch of Gold Denars Stack of Gold Denars Handful of Gold Denars Gold Denar Stack of Silver Denars Handful of Silver Denars Silver Denar Pouch of Gold Denars 100 d Picking up coins puts them straight into your pouch, even with a full inventory. /deco toitem <amount> turns pouch money into coins, and /deco topouch puts the coins in your hand back. To pay someone, drop coins for them to pick up, or use /deco pay <amount> to drop that much at your feet.

Mining stone or deepslate, chopping logs and harvesting fully grown wheat, carrots, potatoes or beetroot sometimes drops a few coins. Fortune makes it more likely. Sell raw goods at a Market Block. Holding Gold Ingots, right-click at your faction's or guild's bank to bank the whole stack at 1 d each. Gold Ingots picked up anywhere else are just gold. Trade with other players, or sign on with a mercenary company. Money you earn, including coins someone else dropped, can be taxed by your faction or guild. The chat line that shows what you earned also shows the tax. Picking up coins you dropped yourself is never taxed.

A Market Block buys raw goods for denars. It only buys: you can't purchase anything from it. Craft a Market Block on a crafting table and place it, or use one someone else placed. Right-click it and pick a category: Metal, Mineral, Stone, Wood, Farm, Fish or Alchemy. Each good shows its current price and a demand bar. Click it to sell one bundle from your inventory. The money goes into your pouch. Prices are shared by every Market Block on the server. Each sale lowers that good's price a little, and demand recovers every 4 hours. A good nobody has sold for a while can pay up to twice its usual price. Food that is no longer fresh sells for less: half when stale, a tenth when rotten. Your inventory has four extra slots for jewellery: one ring, one amulet and two artifacts. Updated 22 Oct 2026
Goldsmiths make rings, necklaces and jewellery artifacts around an infused gemstone, and the quality of the work sets the accessory's stats. See Gem Infusion for every piece and how to make it.

Press E to open your inventory. The first four spaces of the top storage row are accessory slots, so you have four fewer spaces for ordinary items. Drag an accessory onto its slot, or click it in. Slot Takes Ring One ring Amulet One necklace or pendant Artifact (two slots) Medals, mirrors, chalices, bracelets and other jewellery artifacts Each slot only takes its own kind of accessory, and a stacked item cannot be equipped. Note Magic artifacts are a different kind of item and do not fit the Artifact slots.

A faction is a realm on the map: its members, the provinces it claims, its money and its government. The leader runs most of it from /faction menu. Everything belongs to your current character. Updated 23 Oct 2026

The leader sets relations with other factions from the Diplomacy menu. Each faction has an opinion of every other, which slowly moves toward what your relations call for. An alliance needs both sides at 40 or more, a rivalry -10 or less, and a war -50 or less. You can also sign trade agreements and non-aggression pacts, place embargoes, and take smaller factions as subjects. Agreements that need both sides are answered by the other leader with /faction accept while online.

You become the leader of a faction of one. /faction create <name> founds the faction. Stand in an unclaimed province and run /faction setcapital <name> to claim it as your capital. Stand in a chunk of your capital province and run /faction setbank. This is where members pay in and where everyone banks their own money. Invite players with /faction invite <player>.

Government, laws, council and elections are all in /faction menu. Laws set the government type, how the leader is chosen, the council, taxes, the military, vassals, the economy and the borders. Changing a law costs administrative power and locks that law for a few days. When the leader is elected, members vote at a Voting Booth during an election. Only the faction leader can set up a booth. Taxes take a share of what members and guilds earn. Money is settled once a day, and /ledger shows your own daily earnings, taxes and upkeep.

The easiest start is to join a faction that already exists. Ask a faction's leader to invite you. Click Accept on the invite, or type /faction join. /faction list shows every faction. Each faction is split into guilds: you start in the main guild, which the faction leader runs.

Land is claimed one province at a time, and prestige decides how much you can hold. Stand in a province and run /faction claim. It must border your land, or lie across a single stretch of water from it. Sea provinces can't be claimed. Each claim needs prestige: 50 for your second province, 100 for your third, and so on. Prestige isn't spent. Prestige comes mostly from members and the time they play, plus your wealth, trade, land, titles and subjects. Low stability and long inactivity lower it. If your prestige drops too low for the land you hold, other factions can claim your provinces from you. You can hold at most 5 provinces outside a title. Form a County to grow further.

Each faction has a Spymaster, who hides its army and spies on everyone else's. The leader appoints one with /faction spymaster <player>. While nobody is appointed, the leader holds the office. A new Spymaster starts out weak and reaches full strength after a week, and the leader must wait 2 days before appointing someone else, unless the Spymaster's character dies. Your Spymaster hides your military from other factions: your regiments, your faction's vehicles and the military lines of your accounts. Everything else, such as members, money, laws, government, installations and offices, is open to everyone. Each day your Spymaster gathers a report on every other faction's military. It can be a botched report, rumours, or broad, reliable or detailed estimates, and the better it is, the closer its numbers. How good it is depends on both factions' Spymasters. Overlords find it easier to spy on their subjects. The Spymaster can open up your own military to your overlord, your subjects or your allies, so they see it exactly up to the report quality you choose. Set it with /faction spymaster share or in the Spymaster's office in /faction espionage.

The leader forms titles from the Tier menu. Title Formed from Prestige County 5 provinces outside any title 80 Duchy 4 Counties 200 Kingdom 4 Duchies 600 Empire 3 Kingdoms 1,000 Only your highest title adds prestige, on top of 10 for each province. You can't hold more Counties than you have members. Titles that already exist on the map can be claimed from the Titles menu once you hold enough of their provinces. How much depends on your faction's rank: Rank Prestige Provinces needed to claim a title Obscure 0 90% Influential 350 85% Powerful 800 80% Glorious 1,500 75% Legendary 5,000 60% The higher ranks also need a share of the strongest faction's prestige, so they get harder as the top factions grow.

Farms grow two kinds of crops: the usual field crops, such as wheat and potatoes, and 27 custom fruits, vegetables and spices for Cooking and Brewing. Both need open sky, and both grow better in fertile land. Updated 22 Oct 2026

Each custom crop needs a perk from the Forager profession: Fruit Connoisseur, Vegetable Enjoyer or Spice Lover, which all require Farmer first. Spend Forager points on them in /profession. Without the right perk you cannot plant, harvest or break that crop. Plant the seed on farmland. Keep the farmland fully wet (dark). Farmland within 4 blocks of water stays wet, and rain wets the rest for a while. Custom crops stop growing as soon as their farmland starts to dry out. On wet farmland the crop gains a growth step roughly every 10 minutes, so in fertile land a crop ripens in 20 to 50 minutes. Crops only grow while their chunk is loaded. Bone meal sometimes adds a step or two. Right-click a ripe crop with an empty hand to harvest 2 to 4 produce. Crops that regrow drop back to an earlier stage and keep producing. The rest give you a seed back. Breaking a ripe crop always gives its produce and a seed, but removes the plant, even one that would regrow. Breaking an unripe crop loses the seed. Unripe crops can also wither: at a fertility of around 80, about one crop in eight withers before it ripens. Poorer land means slower growth and more losses, and a crop on dry farmland can still wither while it waits. Crops that regrow take the same risk each time they regrow. Apple Banana Cherry Grape Lemon Lime Orange Peach Pineapple Pistachio Plum Strawberry Tomato Corn Cucumber Garlic Lettuce Olive Onion Rhubarb Yeast Basil Black Pepper Cinnamon Nutmeg Spice Leaf Vanilla Loading 3D preview… Apple Perk Fruit Connoisseur Growth steps 5 Regrows Yes

Every province has a fertility from 0 to 100. Switch the map to Fertility to see it. In poor land crops often skip a growth step, and at 0 they do not grow at all. Hardy crops such as nether wart, potatoes and olives cope with poor soil far better than corn or tomatoes. Harvested produce gets a quality of 1 to 5 stars. Fertile land makes good stars more likely, though any result can happen anywhere.

Wheat, potatoes, carrots, beetroots and nether wart are vanilla crops and need no perk. Harvest them by breaking a ripe crop with one of the server's hoes. Every ripe crop in the hoe's area is cut at once, the produce goes into your inventory, and each spot replants itself a moment later. Unripe crops are left alone. Crops broken by hand drop as normal, but their produce is always 1 star. Bone meal does not work on field crops. Hoe Area Chance of +1 star Durability Iron Hoe 1 crop None 600 Steel Hoe 3×3 3.5% 1,200 Abyssalite Hoe 5×5 6% 2,400 Mythril Hoe 7×7 10% 4,800 Each crop harvested costs the hoe 1 durability. Crafting the steel, abyssalite and mythril hoes needs the Hoe Maker perks from the Forager profession. Jumping on farmland does not turn it back to dirt, but it knocks the crop growing on it back to a seedling.

Crops can only be planted outdoors, with nothing but air above them all the way up. Indoors or in a cave you get "Crops must be planted outdoors with open sky above them." Some things above a crop still count as open sky: Glass and glass panes, so greenhouses work. Leaves, logs, vines, fences and gates, lanterns, torches, chains, ladders, banners and hanging signs. Slabs, stairs and signs, but only up to 5 blocks above the crop. A double slab is a roof. Nether wart, mushrooms and yeast can be grown indoors. Building a roof over crops that are already planted does not harm them.

Besides the seeds you get back from harvests, custom seeds come from guild farms. Each focus of a farm or plantation resource node produces its own seeds: Node focus Seeds Vegetable Farm Corn, Cucumber, Lettuce, Rhubarb Onion Farm Garlic, Onion Exotic Farm Olive, Tomato Yeast Production Yeast Fruit Orchard Apple, Grape, Peach, Pistachio, Plum, Strawberry Exotic Fruit Orchard Banana, Cherry, Lemon, Lime, Orange, Pineapple Spice Plantation Basil, Black Pepper, Spice Leaf Sweet Spice Plantation Cinnamon, Nutmeg, Vanilla
Cast into water and wait for a bite. What you can catch depends on the biome and on your rod, and the more valuable catches make you win a short minigame first. Updated 22 Oct 2026

Most catches, such as fish, fragments and music discs, go straight to you. Act materials, animal materials and pottery sherds start a minigame when they bite. Win it to land the catch. If you lose, it gets away. The minigame is harder with a better rod: Easy on an Iron Rod, then Normal, Hard and Very hard on a Mythril Rod. Fishing levels the Forager profession. Time of day and weather make no difference.

A plain vanilla fishing rod counts as an Iron Rod. The other rods and all four hooks are made at the Fishing Station and need the Fisher perk. Buy it with Forager points in /profession, the same menu as the farming perks. Rods cannot be repaired, and enchantments do nothing for fishing in water. To fit a hook, pick it up in your inventory and right-click the rod with it. Right-click the rod again to take the hook off. A hook works on any rod, and the rod's lore shows how many uses the hook has left. Rod Rod durability Hook Hook uses Bite wait, rod and hook Iron Rod 500 Iron Hook 250 ×1.2 Steel Rod 1,000 Steel Hook 500 ×0.5 Abyssalite Rod 2,000 Abyssalite Hook 1,000 ×0.25 Mythril Rod 3,000 Mythril Hook 1,500 ×0.05 A bite normally takes 5 to 30 seconds. Rods and hooks shorten that wait (the Iron Rod alone lengthens it by 30%), but it is never under 2 seconds or over 60. With a Mythril Rod and Mythril Hook, every bite comes at 2 seconds. Oceans, rivers and beaches give fish, including four custom fish for each kind of water, plus ore and disc fragments, music discs and animal materials. Better rods give better-quality animal materials, and some act materials can only be caught with a steel or abyssalite rod. Water in land biomes, such as a forest pond or a swamp, gives that biome's blocks, mob drops, fragments and pottery sherds. These are the same for every rod. Custom fish come out as Cooking seafood with a size and a quality set by your rod: 1–2 stars on an Iron Rod, 2–3 on Steel, 3–4 on Abyssalite and 4–5 on Mythril. Cut them up on a cutting board for one portion per 25 cm of fish, up to six.
Cookware, troughs, tool shelves and display stands are furniture you place in the world and put items into. Most of them are used for cooking. Updated 22 Oct 2026

Placing: hold the piece and right-click the floor. It faces you, and you can't turn it afterwards. The Tool Shelf goes on a wall, the Meat Hook on a ceiling, and the Fire Pit inside a Campfire or Soul Campfire. Filling: right-click a slot with an item to put one in. Right-click it with an empty hand to take it back out. Carrying: the Frying Pan, Saucepan, Pot, Bowl, Butter Plate, Plate, Bread Tray and Trough can be moved. Sneak and right-click with an empty hand to lift one, then right-click a block to set it down, or an Oven Top to slide it in. Picking up: empty the piece and your hand, then right-click it without sneaking. A Fire Pit or oven can't be picked up while something sits on it. Punching a piece, or breaking the block under it, drops it along with whatever is inside.
Blank gemstones are infused with a stat at an Enchanting Table. Infused gems go into the sockets of forged gear, or a goldsmith can set one in a piece of gold jewellery. Updated 22 Oct 2026

Goldsmith perk Jewellery needs the Goldsmith perk (2 Crafter points). It also unlocks the goldsmith tools at the Tool Station. Gold ore can drop Rough, Moldable and Shiny Gold when mined. The Gold Digger perk, which needs Goldsmith, makes those drops more likely. Right-click an empty Smithing Table and pick a project. The menu shows how many gold materials it takes and its tier. Right-click with gold to add it one piece at a time, then with one infused gem. Which golds you use is up to you, but the right mix scores better. Once all the gold and the gem are in, left-click with the hammers and the tinker hammer. Not every piece needs all three. Left-click with the Goldsmith Branding Tool to finish. The piece drops on the bench. Right-click with it to see your progress, or sneak and left-click to cancel and get your gold and gem back. When you finish, you see your Recipe, Hits and Total percentages and the quality, from Rusted up to Masterwork. Better work and a higher tier keep more of the gem's stat. Benches in progress survive restarts. If someone breaks a bench, the gold and gem go to whoever broke it. Golden Key The Golden Key needs no gem, but it has to be made exactly: the right gold mix and the right hits. Anything else ruins it and the gold is lost. Anyone can infuse. You need blank gemstones and an Infusion Ticket, and any Enchanting Table will do. Ordinary vanilla gems don't work. Right-click the table with a blank gem to put it in. A batch holds up to 10. Hold the ticket and left-click the table five times. The batch locks after the first hit, and the fifth uses up one ticket. The infused gems pop out above the table. A Legendary gem is announced to the whole server. Each infused gem rolls a stat and gets a rarity name from how good the roll is, such as Legendary Infused Ruby. It also gets a Success Rate for socketing. Bigger batches lower the best rate a gem can get. A gem only fits its own socket type: Basic, Polished, Radiant or Mythical. Forged gear gets its socket from its quality. Taking a gem out of a socket gives it back with its name and rarity. If you get a gem that was reset to blank, right-clicking a table with it restores it rather than infusing it again.
