How to get from the server address to your first day as a character. Each step links to the page with the details. Updated 23 Oct 2026

/activity opens your activity menu. Each day it deals you a set of hidden tasks, such as voting, playing for an hour or cooking dishes. Click a task to reveal it, because only revealed tasks earn points. Points fill your weekly bar. Each time the bar reaches a reward, claim it in the same menu. The bar starts again every Monday. /vote lists the voting sites.

When you reach the main server, Minecraft asks you to accept its resource pack. Accept it, and the character screen opens once the pack has loaded. If it does not load, set Server Resource Packs to Enabled for the server in your multiplayer list (select it and click Edit), then join again. The character screen opens every time you join. With no character yet, it offers Create character. The creator has several screens, from name, class and race to a short description and clues, so set aside some time. When you finish, click Play. Creating a character

You need to link your Discord account before you can play. You can already do it in the Lobby, and the character screen on the main server has a Link Discord to play button. You can create a character before you link, but you cannot play one until you have. How to link

/rpcharacter kit starter gives each new character a starter kit. What it holds By default, what you type is spoken by your character, and only people nearby hear it. Use /ooc <message> to talk out of character to everyone online. Chat channels Some regions are permadeath zones, and you are warned when you enter one. Read how death works before you travel far. Death and permadeath /helpop <message> reaches the staff and helpers who are online. For anything else, open a ticket in the Discord. Tips show up in chat now and then, and /tfmc tips disable turns them off.
Connect with Minecraft: Java Edition to this address. You arrive in the Lobby. Join the TFMC Discord as well. You need it to link your account, and it has the server lore and announcements.

sectionTitle: The Lobby and the rules quiz
text: Read the server rules, then type /rulequiz in the Lobby. The questions appear in chat one at a time, and you answer by typing in chat. If you make too many mistakes, you have to wait before you can try again. Passing makes you a Commoner. Then right-click the TFMC Roleplay figure to queue for the main server. Next to it, TFMC Tutorial takes you to the Tutorial world at any time, even before the quiz. It explains the server's features and lets you try them out. Characters and items from the Tutorial do not carry over to the main server.
Guilds are the trading houses inside a faction. They earn its trade income, own its resource nodes and use its installations. Updated 23 Oct 2026

Command Aliases What it does Notes /guild menu None Opens your guild. None /guild list None Lists guilds. None /guild create <name> None Founds a guild inside your faction, with you as its leader. Not for the faction leader, or if you already lead or belong to another guild. /guild invite <player> None Invites a player to your guild. Guild leader. Under Open Borders you can invite players from outside the faction. /guild join <name> None Accepts a guild invite. None /guild leave None Leaves your guild and puts you back in your faction's main guild. A guild leader must delete the guild first. To leave the faction, use /faction leave. /guild decline <guild> None Turns down a guild invite, or an offer to lead a guild. None /guild kick <player> None Removes a member, who goes back to your faction's main guild. Guild leader. /guild appoint <guild> <character> None Offers a guild whose leader has died to a living member of your faction. Faction leader. /guild lead <guild> None Accepts an offer to lead a guild. None /guild setleader <player> None Hands the guild to another member. Guild leader. /guild delete <guild> None Disbands your guild. Its members return to the faction's main guild. Guild leader. The bank must be empty, with no loans and no bankruptcy. /guild setcapital [name] None Makes the province you stand in the guild's capital, where its trade starts. Guild leader, in your faction's land. Give a name if the province has no settlement yet. /guild setbank None Makes the chunk you stand in the guild bank. Guild leader. It must be in the guild's capital province. /guild deposit <amount> None Pays money from your pouch into the guild bank. At the guild bank. /guild withdraw <amount> None Takes money from the guild bank into your pouch. Guild leader, at the guild bank. /guild rename <name> /guild setbanner, /guild setcolour <R,G,B> Renames the guild, or sets its banner from your hand or its colour. Guild leader. /faction construct <fort|port|airport|train_station> <name> None Starts building an installation in the province you stand in. Faction leader. Starts at once, with no confirmation. /faction upgrade <installation> None Starts building the next level of a train station. Faction leader. /faction deconstruct [installation] None Demolishes an installation, or cancels one being built. Faction leader. /faction vehicle transfer <installation|pool> None Berths a vehicle at an installation, or gives it to the faction's vehicle pool. Faction leader. The owner must be close by and accept. /faction vehicle take /faction vehicle give <player> Takes a faction vehicle as your own, or gives it to a player. Faction leader. /faction vehicle handover <player> None Offers one of your own vehicles to another player. None /faction vehicle maintenance pay bank None Then right-click a vehicle to pay one day of its upkeep from your bank. None /faction findvehicles <installation> None Lists the vehicles berthed at an installation and where they are. Faction leader.

Every faction member belongs to exactly one guild. Every faction has a main guild, run by the faction leader. You are in it until you found or join another. Any member except the faction leader can found a guild with /guild create <name>. It is free, and you become its leader. A guild has its own leader, banner, capital and bank. Set the capital with /guild setcapital <name>, then the bank inside it with /guild setbank. Any member can pay in; only the guild leader can take money out. From /guild menu, a guild builds up branches. Guild Halls make its trade power and only other guilds have them; the main guild has a Bureaucracy instead. Workshops raise production, Storehouses carry trade further, and Counting Houses lower trade upkeep. A guild can run one resource node, paid for from the guild bank.

Forts, ports, airports and train stations, built by the faction leader in an owned land province. Type Upkeep / day Build time Vehicle slots Fort 30 d 5 days 8 emplacements, 2 land vehicles Port 15 d 3 days 8 ships Airport 20 d 3 days 10 aircraft Train station 5 d 3 days 2 emplacements /faction construct starts building at once, with no confirmation, and costs nothing to start. Only one build can run at a time, and each province takes one of each type. A port must be within 20 blocks of the sea or a river. Upkeep comes from the faction bank. If it can't be paid, the installation loses a level, and one at level 1 is removed. Train stations can be upgraded: level 2 costs 35 d a day (3-day build, 3 emplacements) and level 3 costs 100 d a day (5-day build, 4 emplacements). Trains can't be berthed anywhere.

Installations, and the sea lanes and railways between them, carry trade further. Trade can join a sea lane or railway at any province along it, and is strongest getting on and off at an installation. Guilds can use every installation in their own realm. Abroad, they get the better of two things: what a trade agreement gives, or what the two realms' economy laws allow. A trade agreement gives full use both ways. An unequal treaty gives the stronger side full use and the weaker side half. Embargo or war closes them completely. Economy law Open to foreign guilds Own guilds abroad Free Trade 50% +10% Decentralized 35% None Mercantilism 15% +20% Protectionism 10% None Isolationism Closed -25% The host's law sets how open it is, and the guest's law adds to or takes from that, up to 100%. A closed host stays closed to the guest's law, but not to a trade agreement.

Vehicles cost a little upkeep every day. Each account can own 3 vehicles; train cars don't count. Each one's daily upkeep comes from its owner's bank, not the pouch. An unpaid vehicle slowly loses health, though it never sinks or falls, and it can't be repaired. Pay a day with /faction vehicle maintenance pay bank, then right-click the vehicle. The faction leader can berth a vehicle at an installation or put it in the faction's pool, with its owner close by to accept. The faction bank then pays its upkeep.
Guns are put together from parts at the Gunsmithing Station. Anyone can build one, but only a Musketeer can fire it. Updated 23 Oct 2026

Ammunition is made at the Alchemy Station from one ingot, with no perk needed. Add one Gunpowder to make the Powered version, which hits a little harder. Better metal hits harder and gets more of each hit through armour (for Spreadshot: more pellets that fly further), but you get fewer rounds per ingot. Ammunition Fired by From 1 Iron Ingot From 1 Steel Ingot From 1 Bronze Ingot From 1 Mythril Ingot Shot Rifles and pistols 64 Iron Shot 32 Steel Shot 16 Bronze Shot 8 Mythril Shot Spreadshot Shotguns 32 Iron Spreadshot 16 Steel Spreadshot 8 Bronze Spreadshot 4 Mythril Spreadshot Rocket Launchers 8 Iron Rocket 4 Steel Rocket 2 Bronze Rocket 1 Mythril Rocket Rifled barrels take Iron or Steel Shot and smoothbore barrels only Iron Shot. Bronze and Mythril Shot only fit a rifle with the Experimental Arclock. Spreadshot and Rockets of every metal fit any shotgun or launcher.

Craft the Gunsmithing Station on a crafting table and place it on the floor. Right-click it without sneaking. The Gun Assembly menu opens on a rifle. Click the button in the top-left corner to switch between rifle, pistol, shotgun and launcher. Each part slot already holds a part you are able to make. Click a slot to pick a different part. A barrier means you can't make any part for that slot yet. Pistols and launchers always show one in the stock slot, because they take no stock. Click the finished gun on the right. The materials for all its parts are taken from your inventory at once. Which parts you can use depends on your Smith perks from the Crafter profession, the same perks that unlock metals and woods for Advanced Crafting: Iron Smith for iron parts and oak stocks, Steel Smith for steel and maplewood, Abyssalite Smith for abyssalite and elderwood, and Mythril Smith for mythril and demonwood. Gun Parts Lowest perk Rifle Barrel, loader, chamber, action and stock. Iron Smith Pistol Barrel, loader, chamber and action. No stock. Iron Smith Shotgun Spread Barrel, loader, chamber, action and stock. Steel Smith Launcher Launcher Barrel, loader, chamber and Rocketlock. No stock. Abyssalite Smith The gun is named after its parts (a Matchlock Musket, a Steamlock Pistol, a Blunderbuss) and its look comes from its action, or from its barrel for shotguns and launchers. Its tooltip lists its stats and the ammunition it takes.

Hold the gun in your main hand with its ammunition in your inventory. When it is empty, right-click to reload. It loads as many rounds as it holds, or as many as you carry. Moving while you reload slows it down. Switching to another hotbar slot stops the reload and gives the ammo back. Right-click to fire. Revolvers and Quad Shot launchers fire several times before they need reloading. Sneak and right-click to choose which ammunition the next reload uses. If you run out of that kind, the reload fails until you choose another. Only one gun of each type stays loaded. Firing one unloads your other guns of the same type and gives their ammo back. Bullets drop over distance and fly through leaves and glass without breaking them. A shot to a player's head does extra damage. Shot and rockets push part of each hit straight through armour. Rockets explode when they hit something and hurt everyone nearby, you included, but they never break blocks. Your Charisma tightens your aim and speeds up your reloads.

A part's exact stats show in the Gun Assembly menu. Better metal and wood generally means a better gun. Part Fits Perk Cost Notes Smoothbore Barrel (Long) Rifle Iron Smith 4 Iron Ingot Fires Iron Shot. Rifled Barrel (Long) Rifle Steel Smith 4 Steel Ingot Fires Iron or Steel Shot, and aims better than smoothbore. Smoothbore Barrel (Short) Pistol Iron Smith 4 Iron Ingot Fires Iron Shot. Rifled Barrel (Short) Pistol Steel Smith 4 Steel Ingot Fires Iron or Steel Shot, and aims better than smoothbore. Spread Barrel Shotgun Steel Smith 4 Steel Ingot Fires Spreadshot of any metal. Makes the gun a shotgun. Launcher Barrel Launcher Abyssalite Smith 4 Abyssalite Ingot Fires Rockets of any metal. Makes the gun a launcher. Muzzle Loader All Iron Smith 2 Iron Ingot The basic loader. Breech Loader Rifle, Shotgun, Launcher Mythril Smith 2 Mythril Ingot Reloads much faster. Single Shot Rifle, Pistol, Shotgun Iron Smith 2 Iron Ingot Holds 1 shot. Single Shot (launcher) Launcher Abyssalite Smith 2 Abyssalite Ingot Holds 1 rocket. Shown in game as Single Shot. Quad Shot Launcher Mythril Smith 2 Mythril Ingot Holds 4 rockets. Revolver Rifle, Pistol Abyssalite Smith 2 Abyssalite Ingot Holds 6 shots, but reloads slowly and hits a little softer. Steamlock Rifle, Pistol Iron Smith 2 Iron Ingot Fires plain Iron Shot only, whatever the barrel. No smoke or muzzle flash, and a little less damage. Matchlock Rifle, Pistol, Shotgun Steel Smith 2 Steel Ingot The basic firing action. Flintlock Rifle, Pistol, Shotgun Abyssalite Smith 2 Abyssalite Ingot Aims and fires a little better than the Matchlock. Rocketlock Launcher Abyssalite Smith 2 Abyssalite Ingot The launcher's action. Experimental Arclock Rifle Mythril Smith 2 Mythril Ingot Fires only Bronze or Mythril Shot, whatever the barrel. Very accurate, but slow to fire and reload. Oak Stock Rifle, Shotgun Iron Smith 2 Refined Barkwood Steadies your aim. Maplewood Stock Rifle, Shotgun Steel Smith 2 Refined Maplewood Steadies your aim more. Elderwood Stock Rifle, Shotgun Abyssalite Smith 2 Refined Elderwood Steadies your aim even more. Demonwood Stock Rifle, Shotgun Mythril Smith 2 Refined Demonwood Steadies your aim the most.
Some provinces are overrun by monsters. Walk into one and they keep coming at you, day and night. Fight a wave at a Lure and win, and the province is cleared. Updated 23 Oct 2026
Command What it does /lure leave Gives up the Lure fight you joined, so leaving the province no longer hurts you.

sectionTitle: Clearing a province with a Lure
text: Make a Lure at the Block Station from 2 Oak Planks. You need to be playing a character to place or join one. Place the Lure on the ground inside an infested province. You join its fight automatically. It does nothing in a province that isn't infested, and each province can only have one Lure at a time. Everyone in the province gets 20 seconds to decide: right-click the Lure to join, or leave the province. Then the wave starts: 20, 40, 60 or 80 monsters from Mild to Extreme, let out over about two minutes. Monsters already roaming the province join the wave, and the normal spawning stops until the fight ends. The label above the Lure counts how many are left. Right-click the Lure during the fight to make the remaining monsters glow for 10 seconds. There is no time limit. Kill the last monster and the province is cleared. If everyone who joined dies, gives up or stays logged out, the infestation stays. Warning Once a fight starts, nobody can stand by and watch: If you are in the province and haven't joined, you lose a heart every second. You can still join by right-clicking the Lure. If you joined and then leave the province, you lose a heart every second until you come back or give up with /lure leave. If you joined and log out, you have 5 minutes to come back. After that you are out of the fight, and that character dies the next time you play it, unless the others have won by then. The Lure can't be broken while it is in use, and it disappears when the fight ends, win or lose. A fight still running at the daily restart is lost, with no penalty for anyone.

While you are in an infested province, monsters keep spawning around you, a little way off rather than right next to you. The worse the infestation, the more of them and the faster they come. They don't spawn below Y 56. You get ghouls, rats, slime cubes and skeletons, and bug-like creatures that burst into parasitic worms when they die. The worms bite through armour and poison you.

Every infestation is in bog provinces, mostly in and around the Westmarshes, overrun by Bog Monsters. On the website map, pick the Infestation map mode: each infested province is coloured by how bad it is, from yellow to dark red, and hovering over it names the level. There are four levels: Mild, Worrying, Severe and Extreme. Left alone, an infestation slowly gets worse and can spread into neighbouring bog provinces, even ones that were cleared before.

Lock your doors with a key and choose who can open your chests. You need to be playing a character for any of it. Updated 23 Oct 2026
Command What it does /thievery clearclues Then right-click one of your doors or containers within 30 seconds to wipe the clues left at it.

Any chest, barrel or other container you place is yours, and so are armour stands, item frames, artifact displays and pedestals. They start out Public. Sneak and left-click one to change who can use it. Each click moves to the next setting: Setting Who can use it Private Only you. Guild You and everyone in your guild. Faction Every guild in your faction. Public Anyone. Guild and faction mean your guild and its faction. Your other characters count as strangers. Nobody can break a container they can't open, or turn your chest into a double chest with theirs. Hoppers only move items between containers that have the same owner. Ender chests are not part of this: everyone sees only their own.

Pick up the first item in your inventory and click it onto the second. No station is needed. You can make one paper copy of the same key every 4 hours. Pick up Click onto You get Clay Ball Iron Key or Golden Key Key Mold. The clay is used up. Copper Ingot Key Mold Copper Key. It works like the original. The mold is used up. Paper Iron Key, Golden Key or Copper Key Paper Key. It opens the door once and then falls apart. It can't lock or unlock.

Make an Iron Key at the Tool Station from 2 Iron Ingots. A goldsmith can make a Golden Key, which is harder to pick. Hold the key, sneak and right-click a door, trapdoor or fence gate to lock it. Do it again to unlock. Iron doors and iron trapdoors are the only ones that can't be locked. A locked door only opens for its key or a copy, though anyone can close a locked door or gate. Only someone holding the original key, a Copper Key copy, or a key chain with either can break it, or the block under it. A Key Chain (Tool Station, 2 Iron Ingots) holds up to 5 keys and opens their doors, but it can't lock or unlock. Click a key onto it to add it, and right-click the chain in your inventory to take the last key off.

A lock stops most people, but someone with a lockpick can still get in: Your locks can only be picked while you, or someone from the guild the lock belongs to, is online, and for a short while after. A Faction lock lets your whole faction in, but a thief who picks one can carry off much more than from a Private or Guild lock. Thieves often leave clues behind. You can wipe the clues at your own door or container with the command below, though you may want to read them first.

A mage weapon is built from parts at a Magic Station, attuned to a school with an Enchanted Charge, and fitted with spell runes. Only the Mage class can use one. What Resonance and the schools are is explained on Magic. Updated 23 Oct 2026

A weapon with no school in it cannot cast anything. Fill an Enchanted Charge at a shrine. Its tooltip then shows a tier for each school it holds, such as Cerrith II. Hold the charge and right-click the weapon on its station. The charge is used up straight away, and orbs start circling the station. Look at an orb and left-click to hit it. Hit the pale blue orbs: chat tells you how many you need, and every one that fades before you hit it loses part of the charge. Avoid the rust-orange ones, which add Rift to the weapon. Higher-tier charges have faster orbs and fewer good ones. When time runs out, chat shows the tier the weapon reached and how much of the charge it kept. If you disconnect, the run ends and the weapon keeps what it had caught so far. Right-click the station with an empty hand. The weapon pops out on top of it. Don't leave a finished weapon on a station. A charge stronger than you If the charge is above your own Resonance in a school, a warning lists what you are missing. Right-click again within a few seconds to use it anyway. You still can't cast those spells until your Resonance catches up. Rift is the chance that a cast fizzles. The weapon's tooltip shows it as a percentage.

Hold the weapon in either hand and use the rune's key. Most runes cast with right-click, and a few use left-click or sneak and left-click. To change a rune's key, hold the rune and use /magic rune keybind. Carry only one staff: with two or more anywhere in your inventory, every cast fizzles. What you see Why Cost *Whiff* The weapon's Rift made the cast fizzle, or you carry more than one staff. Mana and cooldown. *Refused* Your Resonance or the weapon's attunement is below the spell's tier, or the weapon was never attuned to that school. Chat says which. Nothing. *Worn out* The weapon is on its last point of durability. Nothing, but it won't cast or fire until repaired. *Damaged* The weapon holds runes that no longer fit. Right-click an empty station with it to get the loose runes back. Nothing, but it won't cast until fixed. Every spell you cast, including a whiff, uses a little of the weapon's durability, and so does every wand bolt. A blade also wears when you hit with it. A mage weapon never breaks: it stops at Worn out. A Magical Repair Kit dragged onto it restores durability, and works on Mage Armour too.
Command Aliases What it does /magic rune keybind <key> None While holding a spell rune, changes the key that casts it: RIGHT_CLICK, LEFT_CLICK, SHIFT_RIGHT_CLICK or SHIFT_LEFT_CLICK.

sectionTitle: From parts to your first spell
text: Build a staff, wand or blade at a Magic Station. Make an Enchanted Charge at a Rune Station and fill it at a shrine. Use the charge on the weapon to attune it, then take the weapon off the station. Get a spell rune by researching a blank runestone, and put it into one of the weapon's sockets. Raise your own Resonance by meditating, then cast.

Raise a weapon's attunement, or wipe it and start over. Recharge: hold the weapon and right-click an empty station to set it down, then use another charge on it. A later charge can add schools and raise them, but never lowers one. It also cleans some Rift off the weapon. Re-attune: hold the weapon, sneak and right-click an empty station. Chat shows the fee, half the materials of the weapon's parts, rounded up. Sneak and right-click again to pay. The next charge that catches anything replaces the old attunement and its Rift. Your runes stay in place. While a re-attune is waiting, only you can charge the weapon or take it back. To call it off, sneak and left-click the station when no charge is running. You get the weapon and the fee back.

Turns Enchanted Dust into runestones, Enchanted Charges and sealed artifacts. Each craft takes 10 seconds. Rune Station Crafting Table Requires: None Blackstone Blackstone Blackstone Blackstone Gold Ingot Blackstone Blackstone Blackstone → Rune Station Place it, then right-click it to make runestones and Enchanted Charges from Enchanted Dust. Size Runestone Armor Runestone Enchanted Charge Minor 4 dust 16 dust 4 dust Lesser 8 dust 32 dust 8 dust Greater 12 dust 48 dust 12 dust Ascendant 16 dust 64 dust 16 dust Runestones are blank. To turn one into a rune, hold it and right-click a Lectern to start a Research project. Finishing it gives a random spell rune of the same size from any of the four schools. An armor runestone gives a random armour rune instead. Sealed artifact Cost Sealed Artifact 18 dust Sealed Cerrith Artifact 28 dust Sealed Oseni Artifact 28 dust Sealed Seithr Artifact 28 dust Sealed Mitlan Artifact 28 dust Right-click a sealed artifact to break the seal. The plain one holds a random artifact, and the others a random artifact of their school.

A socket takes a rune of its own size or smaller, never a bigger one. Drag a rune onto the weapon or armour in your inventory to set it. An Unsocket Tool, made at the Tool Station, takes runes back out. Every spell comes from a rune, so a weapon with no runes casts nothing. A smaller rune in a bigger socket works, but it uses that socket up. A rune goes into the smallest free socket that can hold it. Spell runes only fit mage weapons. Armour runes only fit Mage Armour, where they add mana or protection. Mage Armour is forged at the Forging Station. Its socket size comes from the quality of the craft, not the metal, so a Masterwork iron piece takes an Ascendant armour rune.

A vanilla 3x3 craft that anyone can make. Magic Station Crafting Table Requires: None Blackstone Blackstone Blackstone Blackstone Gold Ingot Blackstone Blackstone Amethyst Shard Blackstone → Magic Station Place it, then right-click it to open the weapon assembly menu. Place the station and right-click it with an empty hand. Choose Staff, Wand or Sword (the Mage Blade), then pick the parts. Building takes the materials from your inventory. The new weapon rests on the station, unattuned, and stays there until a charge is used on it. Changed your mind? Sneak and left-click the station to take the weapon apart and get the materials back. A charge already used on it is lost.

The core decides how many rune slots the weapon gets. Weapon How it fights Rune slots by core Mage Staff Two-handed. No melee attack. Iron 1, Steel 2, Abyssalite 3, Mythril 4 Mage Wand No melee attack. Left-click fires a bolt that costs mana. Iron 1, Steel 1, Abyssalite 2, Mythril 2 Mage Blade A sword with normal melee hits. Iron 1, Steel 1, Abyssalite 2, Mythril 2 Every weapon needs a core and a handle. Each extra slot the core opens up needs a tome. The handle and each tome give one socket, and their grade sets its size: Handle or tome Socket Oak Magical Handle, Simple Magical Tome Minor Basic Magical Handle or Tome Lesser Petty Magical Handle or Tome Greater Heavy Magical Handle or Tome Ascendant Simple Tome (made without dust) None A better core also gives the weapon more durability, and on a wand or blade it hits harder. The weapon is named after its core, for example Steel Mage Staff. Part costs are listed under Materials.

Mages cast spells from runes set into a weapon they build themselves. Each spell belongs to a school of magic, and it only works if both you and your weapon are strong enough in that school. This page covers the schools, your own magical skill and how to raise it. Building, charging and using the weapon is on Mage Weapons. Updated 23 Oct 2026

Artifacts are what you meditate with, so look after them. An artifact's tooltip lists how much aura it holds in each school. Aura stored in an artifact never fades on its own, but two things reduce what it gives you. Muffling. An artifact holding aura becomes muffled while it sits in a chest or any other container, and a muffled artifact gives less when you meditate. Its tooltip shows a Muffled percentage. Keep artifacts in your inventory, on a Pedestal, on an Artifact Display or in an item frame. There they slowly recover. Use. Every bit of Resonance an artifact gives anyone wears it out. Once it has been used, its tooltip shows its Integrity. At the end it crumbles into a spent husk with no aura, which only the Recycler will take.

Only the Mage class can use Mage Staffs, Mage Wands, Mage Blades and Mage Armour. Mage gear is expensive, so plan for the cost. There are four schools: Cerrith, Oseni, Seithr and Mitlan. Each has its own spells, shrines and Resonance. Your magic belongs to your character. A second character starts from nothing, and /resonance only opens while you play a character. Term What it means Resonance Your skill in one school, from 0 to 100. You raise it by meditating. Aura Magical energy of one school. Shrines fill artifacts and charges with it. Artifact A magical object that stores aura. You meditate with artifacts to gain Resonance. Enchanted Charge A single-use item you fill at a shrine and then spend to attune a mage weapon. Equilibrium Your balance between Corruption and Tranquility. Casting and meditating move it. Mental Points Your focus. Meditation and Research both use it up.

Pick a cast mode in /resonance. Flow is the default. Every spell you cast moves your Equilibrium: toward Corruption in Surge and toward Tranquility in Flow. Both sides make your spells cheaper, stronger or quicker to recharge, and the effect grows the further you go. Corruption pays off early. Once you have some, it keeps growing on its own, faster the deeper you are, and its bonus weakens again near the extreme. Tranquility has to build up before it helps much, but its bonus ends up stronger. It slowly fades back toward the middle if you stop.
Command Aliases What it does /resonance /res Opens your Resonance screen: your Resonance in each school, your Equilibrium, your Mental Points and the Surge or Flow choice.

Meditating in a ring of artifacts is how you raise your Resonance. Place 8 pedestals around a centre block, level with it: one 4 blocks north, south, east and west, and one on each diagonal, 3 blocks across and 3 blocks along. The ring does not need to be a shrine. Put artifacts on the pedestals. You gain Resonance in the schools those artifacts hold. Sit on the centre block, for example with /sit. Meditation starts by itself. A white orb appears where you are looking. Look at it and left-click to begin. More orbs then circle you. Each one you hit raises your Resonance and uses one Mental Point. Blue orbs move your Equilibrium toward Tranquility and red orbs toward Corruption. Hitting a red orb makes you lose focus, and only red orbs appear for a few seconds. Stand up to stop. Message What it means Can't meditate here, no artifacts None of the pedestals holds an artifact with aura. Nothing to gain from meditating here You already have as much Resonance as this ring can give you in every school it holds. Meditation complete at this site You reached that limit during this sitting. You are too tired to meditate now You are out of Mental Points. Come back once they refill. A ring can only raise you as high as your share of its aura. Everyone who has recently meditated with an artifact shares it, so a ring used by several mages gives each of them less.

Your focus, shown in /resonance. A new character starts full. Every orb you hit while meditating uses one, and so does every Research experiment. Both draw from the same pool. They refill a little every hour, even while you are offline. Wisdom and Intelligence make them refill faster. A Focus Potion restores 50. Potion Brewers make them at the Alchemy Station.

Open /resonance to see your Resonance in each school, from 0 up to 100. Every spell has a tier from I to IV, and the size of its rune tells you which: a Minor rune holds a tier I spell, a Lesser rune tier II, a Greater rune tier III and an Ascendant rune tier IV. To cast a spell, your Resonance in its school must reach that tier, and so must your weapon's attunement in that school. Higher tiers need more Resonance. A new character has none, so even tier I spells need some meditation first. If a spell is beyond you, chat tells you the tier it needs and the tier you have, for example "This spell needs Cerrith II. You carry I." Low Resonance makes a school's spells cost more mana, deal less damage and take longer to recharge. High Resonance does the opposite. Hover a school in /resonance to see how it affects you right now. Resonance slowly fades while you are online. Time spent offline does not count.

A shrine fills artifacts and Enchanted Charges with aura. A shrine is a Pedestal and everything within 4 blocks of it in every direction, above and below included. Build that space with blocks that suit a school. A mix of different fitting blocks works better than a lot of one kind. Each school is scored on its own, so one shrine can serve more than one. Put an artifact or a charge on the pedestal and it slowly fills with aura. A blank charge first takes on every school the shrine gives. "This shrine holds nothing for the charge" means the shrine is not strong enough in any school yet. A shrine can only fill up to its own strength, so a weak shrine never fills a strong charge to the top. "There is no aura to be gathered from this shrine" means it has nothing more to give that item. A pedestal that is part of a meditation ring does not fill anything.

Command Aliases What it does Notes /instruments play None Opens the on-screen keyboard for the instrument you are holding. Right-clicking with the instrument does the same. /instruments keybinds None Lists the notes and chords on each hotbar key for the instrument in your off-hand. None /instruments list None Lists every instrument. None /music help /recording help Lists the recording commands. They do the same as the buttons in the studio. None /music new <title> /music title <title> Starts a new song, or renames the one you have open. None /music projects /music open <id>, /music status Lists your songs, opens one, or shows the tracks of the open song. None /music record <track> /music stop Records a take on track 1 to 4, or stops recording or playback. None /music preview [take] None Plays the whole song. With take, plays your last take with the other tracks. None /music keep /music discard Keeps or throws away your last take. None /music volume <track> <0-2> /music mute <track>, /music remove <track> Sets a track's volume, mutes or unmutes it, or deletes it. None /music bpm <40-240> /music metronome <on|off> Sets the metronome's tempo, or turns the metronome on or off. Recorded notes keep their timing. /music blank None Turns the ordinary music disc in your main hand into a blank recording disc. None /music publish None Records the whole song onto the blank disc in your main hand. None /music copy None Copies the recorded disc in your off-hand onto the blank disc in your main hand. None /music reset confirm None Clears the song you have open. Discs you already published keep it. None

Turn up the Jukebox/Note Blocks volume. Instruments, the keyboard and music discs all use it. For the hotbar, the instrument must be in your off-hand, and slot 9 never plays. The Lute weapon forged in Advanced Crafting is not an instrument and can't be played.

The quickest way to play, and you can keep walking while you do. Put the instrument in your off-hand. Press 1 to 8 to play C, D, E, F, G, A, B and the next C up. Hold Shift for a second layer. Most instruments play a full chord on each key. The Flute, Trumpet and Bagpipe play the same notes an octave higher instead. After each note your selection jumps back to slot 9, so you can play the same note twice. Slot 9 plays nothing, and whatever is in it is what others see in your hand. /instruments keybinds lists every key for the instrument you hold.

Play with the mouse instead of the number keys. Right-click while holding an instrument, or use /instruments play. The keyboard has three rows of notes from C to B: high, middle and low. Click a note to play it. Instruments with chords show a small dot under each note: click it for the chord. The options button changes the keyboard's size.

Record a song in up to four layers and press it onto a music disc. Craft a Music Station at the Instrument Station from 6 Spruce Planks, 4 Glass Panes, 1 Iron Ingot and 1 Black Dye. Place it and right-click it. Stay within a few blocks while you use it. Create a song and give it a title. Each character can keep up to 36 songs; right-click one to delete it. Each row is a track, up to four. Hold an instrument and press record on a track. After a 3-second count-in, play from your hotbar or the keyboard. A take can last up to 3 minutes. Listen to the take with the other tracks, then keep or discard it. Each track has its own volume and mute. Song settings change the title and the metronome, which only you hear and is never recorded. Pick up one music disc and place it on Publish full song. The disc now plays your song in any jukebox, heard within 32 blocks, and shows its title and you as the author. Publishing over a disc that already has a song needs a second click to confirm. Copies made before keep the old version. You can publish once every 30 seconds, and up to 20 new or changed versions across your account in any 24 hours. Publishing an unchanged version again doesn't count. Every studio button also has a /music command, and /music copy copies a recorded disc onto a blank one.
The Recycling Station breaks crafted gear back down into some of the materials that made it. Updated 22 Oct 2026
Made on a crafting table and placed on the floor. Recycling Station Crafting Table Requires: None Iron Ingot Iron Ingot Iron Ingot Iron Ingot Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks → Recycling Station

Right-click the station to open it. Click the item in your inventory to move it in. Click it again in the station to take it back. Items that can't be recycled, or that are unbreakable, are refused. The right side of the menu shows what you would get back. Click the confirm button in the top-left corner. The materials pop out of the station, and anyone nearby can grab them. Gear returns at most half of what went into it, less the more worn it is. Each material is rounded down, so a material that went in only once won't come back, and fully broken gear gives nothing. If nothing would come back, confirming tells you so and you keep the item. If you close the menu with an item still in it, you get the item back. With a full inventory, it waits for your character until you have room.

Item Returns Forged weapons and armour Up to half the materials. An alloy comes back as its base metal or wood and its crystals. Guns Up to half the materials the gun was made from. Broken guns and guns made before tracking began can't. Mage weapons Up to half the materials paid to craft it. Take any runes out first. Broken ones can't. Gold jewellery Up to half the gold. The gem is not returned. Spell runes 2, 4, 6 or 8 Enchanted Dust (Minor to Ascendant). Armour runes 4, 8, 12 or 16 Enchanted Dust (Minor to Ascendant). Artifacts Enchanted Dust by rarity: 4, 8, 12, 16 or 28 (Common to Legendary). Any stored aura is lost. Spent husks Half an artifact's dust: 2, 4, 6, 8 or 14. Unusable Scrap Each material in it has a chance to come back; its tooltip shows the odds. The scrap is used up either way. Vanilla items can't be recycled.

Research is a guessing game played at a Lectern. Every project hides a few aspects, such as Metal or Magic. You test items to find out which aspects they are and fill each one up, and a finished project gives you its result. Updated 23 Oct 2026

Right-click your lectern to open the project. Click an item in your inventory to put it in the test slot. Its preview shows the aspects it carries, how many points it would add to each, and whether each aspect is still Testing, already Confirmed or Rejected. Press Confirm Experiment. The test uses one Mental Point, and you get the item back. Pick the next item from what you learned, and keep going until every aspect is full. An item has a main aspect and sometimes a weaker second one. It adds more points to its main aspect. Each item can be tested only once per project. Items with no aspects can't be tested at all. A hidden aspect first shows as an Undiscovered row. Keep adding points to it until chat says "Aspect confirmed" and the row shows its name. Confirmed is not the same as done, so keep filling it. An aspect the project doesn't use is Rejected after a few tests. An experiment that only adds rejected aspects is refused. Points beyond what an aspect needs are wasted, and a test still costs a Mental Point when it adds nothing. Intelligence makes aspects show up and confirm sooner. On an Unknown Research Paper the result itself stays hidden until you have confirmed enough aspects.

Fill every aspect to finish. When every aspect is confirmed and full, the result drops on top of the lectern. Pick it up quickly, because anyone nearby can. A runestone gives a random rune of its size, and a paper gives a Completed Thesis. Right-click a Completed Thesis to add its entry to your Codex and earn experience. This uses up the thesis. If you already know that entry, you keep the thesis, so you can sell or trade it. Ways to lose a project Breaking the lectern destroys the project. The Scrap button does too, after you confirm it, and nothing is refunded.

A project starts from a research paper or a blank runestone. Sneak and right-click a Cartography Table to open the Research Station. Make a Parchment Paper from a Paper and an Alchemy Powder. Combine the Parchment Paper with a subject, such as an ingot, to get a Research Paper about it. You get the subject item back. Papers you have no ingredients for stay hidden. A Lost Knowledge Fragment instead makes an Unknown Research Paper, which studies a random topic. Every craft here also gives a little Herborist experience. Hold the paper and right-click a Lectern. The paper is used up and the project starts. A blank runestone from the Rune Station starts a project the same way, without a paper. Only the character who started a project can work on it. You can run projects on several lecterns at once, and they survive restarts.
Small tools for setting a scene: sit down, lie down or crawl, pose armor stands, put on a mask, and give your items their own names and lore. Every player can use them. Updated 22 Oct 2026

/tfmc statues gives you the Armor Statues book, free and as often as you need it. Open the book and click an option to change the nearest armor stand within 3 blocks. Use Check Target first: it makes the stand that will be edited glow for a few seconds. Category What you can change Settings Arms, base plate, size, visibility, gravity and visual fire Poses Ready-made poses such as Salute, Facepalm and Stargazing, a random pose, or each limb by hand Position Rotation, small moves, aligning the stand to a block, and scale from 0.25 to 3 times Tools Mirror and flip, copy and paste a pose, swap equipment slots, and undo or redo Locking a stand stops accidental edits and equipment clicks, but it does not protect the stand from other players.

Command Aliases What it does Notes /sit None Sits you down where you stand. None /sit toggle None Turns sitting by right-clicking stairs, slabs, carpets and snow on or off. On by default. /lay /glay Lie down. None /layback /glayback Lie on your back. None /bellyflop /gbellyflop Lie face down. None /spin /gspin Spin around on the ground. None /crawl /gcrawl Drop down and crawl. Double-tapping sneak does not start a crawl here. /tfmc statues None Gives you the Armor Statues book. None /tfmc masks None Gives you a random mask. Once every 10 seconds. /tfmc patterns None Gives you all ten banner patterns. Once every 10 seconds.

Craft them at the Tool Station. Pick the stone up on your cursor and click it onto a single, unstacked item in your inventory, then type your text in chat within 60 seconds, or type cancel. A Lorestone adds a line of lore, and typing clear instead removes all of the item's lore. A Namestone renames the item. If something goes wrong, you get the stone back. A line can be up to 100 characters, colour codes included, and an item can have up to 10 lore lines, counting the ones it already has. Use & colour codes or &#RRGGBB hex colours. If you type a name without colour codes, the namestone offers a palette you can click, or you can type a colour name or a hex value. Lorestone Tool Station Crafting time: 5 seconds Gold Ingot → Lorestone Namestone Tool Station Crafting time: 5 seconds Iron Ingot → Namestone

/tfmc masks gives you a random mask. Most masks hide who you are while you wear them on your head: in-character chat shows you as Masked, and nobody can read your character card. /tfmc patterns gives you all ten banner patterns for the loom: Flower, Guster, Field Masoned, Skull, Thing, Globe, Snout, Flow, Creeper and Bordure Indented. You can use each command once every 10 seconds.

/lay, /layback, /bellyflop and /spin put you in a pose, and /crawl drops you to a crawl. Sneak to get back up. While posed you cannot use blocks, items or other players, so save poses for a quiet moment. Lying down counts towards skipping the night when someone else is in a bed.

Right-click a stair, slab, carpet or snow layer with an empty hand, from up to 3 blocks away, to sit on it. You sit where you clicked, and on stairs you face the way the stair faces. Only the bottom half of stairs and slabs works. You can also type /sit to sit where you stand. Several players can share a block, but you cannot sit on other players. Sneak to stand up. Taking damage does not unseat you, but breaking the block under you does. If you keep sitting down by accident while building, /sit toggle turns click-to-sit off; /sit still works.
Your Minecraft account, your Discord account and the TFMC website work together once they are linked. Updated 23 Oct 2026

Command What it does Notes /linkdiscord Gives you a code to link your Discord account. Run /linkdiscord <code> in the Discord server. You cannot play in Survival until you are linked. /unlinkdiscord Removes your Discord link. You will need to link again to play in Survival. /token create profile Gives you a one-time code to sign in to your profile on the website. None /token create <skin|drink> Gives you a one-time code to upload a custom skin or drink on the website. Noble rank and above. Skin and drink codes share one cooldown. /patreon [unlink] Links your Patreon account, shows your supporter status, or removes the link. None /tfmc patreon Shows the link to the server's Patreon page. None /tfmc tips <enable|disable> Turns the tips shown in chat on or off. None /tfmc pack [auto|manual] Loads the server resource pack now, or sets whether it loads automatically when you join. None /tfmc map Gives you the link to the nations map on the website. None /tfmc date Shows today's weekday and month in the world's own calendar. None /tcore stats <advancedcrafting|factions|rpcharacters|skills|vehicles> Shows your own statistics for that part of the game. None /tfmc drinks Opens the drink builder. Noble rank and above. /tfmc booster Starts a one-hour profession EXP booster for everyone on the server. Ascended and Legacy only, once every 3 days.

Supporter ranks come from Patreon. Run /patreon to link your Patreon account and see your status, and /patreon unlink to remove the link. The Noble, Gilded and Ascended ranks follow your Patreon tier. /tfmc patreon shows the Patreon page.

Run /token create profile in game for a one-time code, then enter it on your profile to sign in. There you can create characters, change their wills, manage wardrobes and kits, and see your custom skins and drinks and your linked accounts.

/token create skin and /token create drink give you a code for uploading a custom skin or drink on the website. They are a supporter perk, and both share one cooldown that depends on your rank. Rank Skin or drink code Commoner Not available Noble Every 28 days Gilded Every 21 days Ascended Every 14 days Legacy Every 7 days

You cannot play in Survival until your Discord account is linked; until then you are held in place. Type /linkdiscord in game to get a code you can click to copy, then run /linkdiscord <code> in the TFMC Discord server. The game confirms the link within a second or so. /unlinkdiscord removes it again. If you leave the Discord server, you have a grace period to rejoin. After that your account is unlinked and you cannot play in Survival until you link again.

Some stations are blocks you craft on a crafting table and place. Others are ordinary blocks, such as a blast furnace or a jukebox, that double as a station. On those, sneak and right-click to open the station, so a plain right-click still uses the block normally. The fletching table and brewing stand open with a plain right-click instead. A recipe can need a profession perk or a class, and most take a few seconds to craft. The recipe card on the station's page shows both. Vehicles from the Engineering Table and Dockyard are the exception: they take hours or days to build. Smithing and tools Station Block Open with What it's for Forging Station Its own block Right-click Smith weapons, armour and bows from metal and wood ingredients. Ingredient Converter Its own block Right-click Turns metals and woods into smithing ingredients and shows the stats they give. Alloy Forge Its own block Right-click Melts metals and catalysts together into named alloys. Ingot Station Blast Furnace Sneak + right-click Smelts ingots and Coke, makes the smithing woods and gemstones, and packs materials into storage blocks. Tool Station Crafting Table Sneak + right-click Tools from iron to Mythril, smithing and goldsmith tools, keys, lockpicks, mount gear and everyday items. Gunsmithing Station Its own block Right-click Builds rifles, pistols, shotguns and launchers from parts you choose. Recycling Station Its own block Right-click Breaks crafted gear, runes, artifacts and scrap back down into materials. Wood, stone and building Station Block Open with What it's for Woodworking Station Its own block Right-click Carves decorative wooden furniture. You need the Artisan perk to use it. Forester Station Fletching Table Right-click Logs, leaves, flowers, dyes, moss, arrows, string and other plant blocks. Block Station Stonecutter Sneak + right-click Building blocks in bulk, such as stone, concrete, mud and ice, plus a few decorations. Copper Station Grindstone Sneak + right-click Every copper block: cut, chiselled, grates, bulbs, doors, lanterns, chests and their waxed forms. Food, animals and fishing Station Block Open with What it's for Meal Prep Station Its own block Right-click Kitchen tools and cookware: knife, pans, pot, oven, fire pit, cutting board and more. Animal Station Its own block Right-click Companion eggs, pet toys and treats, the Trough, the Mount Whistle and spawn eggs. Fishing Station Its own block Right-click Fishing rods and hooks, and turns fished-up fragments and broken discs into finished items. Rune Station Its own block Right-click Turns Enchanted Dust into runestones, Enchanted Charges and Sealed Artifacts. Alchemy Station Brewing Stand Right-click Alchemist Collectors, alchemy powders, health and mana potions, and every kind of gun ammunition. Medicine Station Its own block Right-click Medicines, surgical supplies, prosthetic limbs and the doctor's outfit. Thieves pick locks and pockets, and bandits rob people and loot the graves of those they kill. To protect your own things, see Locks & Keys. Updated 23 Oct 2026

Thief and Bandit are evil archetypes. Once your account is a day old, you can give one or both to a character whose personality fits when you create it. A Thief can pick chests and display furniture and pick pockets. Anyone with a lockpick can pick a door. A Bandit can rob players and loot graves. Warning Lockpicking, pickpocketing, robbing and grave looting each start a 30-minute evil RP session, and doing any of them again starts it over. During a session, any strike you take in a started PvP fight kills your character outright (see death and graves).

Picking a door or display can leave a clue behind, and taking from a chest always does. A clue is one of the clues you wrote for your character or a hint at your race, and once in a while it names you outright. Other characters nearby slowly notice clues until they fade away. Pickpocketing and robbery leave no clues at the scene.

Command What it does /thievery loadout Choose which kinds of items you can see and take. Thief or Bandit. /pickpocket start Then right-click a player within 4 blocks to pick their pocket. Thief only. /robbery start Then right-click a player within 4 blocks to demand a robbery. Bandit only. /robbery accept Accepts a robbery demanded of you. Anyone can use it.

Right-click a locked container as a Thief. You are held in place while you work. A ring of tumblers appears. Press the movement key shown in the middle while the pointer is in the green zone. Set all 4 to open the lock. One slip and it fails. Sneak to give up. The container opens hidden. Click a slot to look at it: the first look is always safe, and each safe slot shows how many seized pins are next to it. Right-click a slot to mark it as a pin. Clicking a pin snaps a lockpick and ends the search, but you can still take what you found. Take the items you uncovered that your loadout lets you see. You or your guild can only pick the same container once every 3 days.

Locked artifact displays, pedestals, armour stands and item frames can be picked as a Thief with a Strong Lockpick, from within 3 blocks, using the same bar as doors. On a success, whatever your loadout lets you see goes straight into your inventory.

Right-click a locked door within 3 blocks. A bar runs across your screen: right-click again when the marker is on green. Red breaks your lockpick, yellow just fails, and walking away cancels. A picked door swings open and stays unlocked for everyone for an hour. A door locked with a Golden Key needs a Strong Lockpick.
A Bandit who kills a player can rob their locked grave without a lockpick. One right-click takes everything your loadout lets you see, as far as your inventory has room.

Before stealing, a Thief or Bandit picks which kinds of items they know how to spot with /thievery loadout. Each kind costs points, and you have 10 at most. Adding a kind uses points that come back at 1 an hour; removing one gives nothing back. Your loadout is shared by all the characters on your account. When you steal, items of kinds you didn't pick show as HIDDEN! and can't be taken. You can only carry off so much each time, so pricey items may not fit at all.

The Basic Lockpick (1 Steel Ingot) and the stronger Strong Lockpick (2 Steel Ingots) are made at the Tool Station. Hold one and right-click what you want to open. When a lockpick breaks, only one from the stack is lost. After a failed try, give it a minute before trying the same lock again.

Run /pickpocket start and right-click someone within 4 blocks. You are held in place. Press jump quickly to fill the ring twice within 30 seconds. Their main inventory opens (not their hotbar or armour). Take what you can, and stay within 4 blocks or it ends. Each pocket you look through may let your mark hear something rummaging in their bag. A botched attempt always gets noticed, and sometimes they see exactly who it was. You or your guild can only pickpocket the same person once an hour.

A robbery is a hold-up both players agree to play out. As a Bandit, run /robbery start and right-click someone within 4 blocks. They have 30 seconds to accept with /robbery accept or the button in chat. Once they accept, they are frozen and can't be hurt or touch their inventory. You get 2 minutes to look through everything they carry, armour included. If your loadout includes money, their coin pouch is there too: click it to take 10 denars, or shift-click for 100. Closing the menu ends the robbery. If your victim logs out during it, everything they carry drops. You or your guild can only rob the same person once every 3 days.

Open /professions and buy Engineer ranks in the Crafter profession. Engineer I costs 1 point for ground vehicles. Engineer II requires I and costs 2 more points for ships. Engineer III requires II and costs 3 more points for aircraft. Craft and place an Engineering Table for land vehicles, fixed guns and aircraft, or a Dockyard for ships. Use the crafting-table patterns below. Right-click the station, choose a category and select a blueprint that your Engineer rank unlocks. Gather its listed materials before selecting the building spot. Left-click the intended spawn point within 12 blocks of the station. Choose it within 30 seconds of selecting the blueprint. The materials are consumed when you choose the spot. Wait for the build to finish. Stay within 96 blocks so the completed vehicle can appear, then right-click it to claim it and select a seat. Collect them before they despawn.

Enter: right-click the vehicle and choose a seat. Shift reopens seat selection while aboard. Only the captain steers. Drive: run /vf keybinds while seated to see the controls for your vehicle. W/S commonly adjusts throttle and A/D steers. Controls can change between ground, flight and water. Refuel: hold the fuel listed on the vehicle page and right-click once per item. Each Coal Block or Arcane Fuel adds 100 fuel units. Stop an Arcane Fuel engine before refuelling; Coal Blocks can be added while an engine runs. Carry cargo: right-click a vehicle with storage to open its containers. Wooden Cart and Cloudskimmer each hold 54 slots. Behemoth has four 54-slot holds. Coal Car holds 27 slots of Coal Blocks. Tow: sneak-right-click a Wooden Cart or Field Artillery, then sneak-right-click a Horse Cart to connect it. Repeat on the towing vehicle to detach. Stay within eight blocks while making the connection. Save fuel by stopping the engine Fuel burns at the same rate at any throttle above or below zero; zero throttle uses none. Locomotive overdrive above 100% burns more. A damaged engine also limits maximum throttle, so repair it to restore power.

Claim a new vehicle by right-clicking it. A claimed vehicle starts with an owner-only whitelist. Open Ownership Settings in Select Seat to allow other players, add a player by name or enable passenger tickets. With tickets enabled, hold Paper and right-click your vehicle to make matching tickets for passengers. Reset Owner releases ownership. Clicking an occupied yellow seat ejects its passenger and prevents re-entry for 60 seconds. Use /vf findvehicles to locate your vehicles. Vehicles more than 160 blocks from players unload into storage; they are not destroyed.

Hold Vehicle Repair and right-click a grounded, stationary vehicle, or use a mechanic seat to repair while aboard. Use the Repair Tool in the menu to fix components and the Water Bucket for fires. Keep the menu open and stay nearby until repair finishes. Hold Vehicle Paint and right-click to open Select Skin. Keep ship pumps repaired to control flooding. Repair damaged engines and wings to recover performance.
Choose a vehicle above, then select one of its available skins beside the preview. In game, use Vehicle Paint to choose from the skins available to you.

Build trains on custom train tracks. Craft Train Track in batches of 64 at the Block Station. Leave room for wide bends and gentle slopes: turns have a 35-degree limit, and slopes have a 10-degree maximum. Choose the seat assigned to a weapon. Hold its ammunition and right-click to reload, then use Space to fire. W/S adjusts elevation and A/D traverses; mounted rifles aim toward your cursor. Check /vf keybinds for the controls of your current seat. Wars between factions are fought as scheduled battles, one evening at a time. You don't need to lead anything to take part: sign up for your side's warband on a battle day. Updated 23 Oct 2026

All times are Paris time (CET/CEST). Battles start the day after war is declared, at most one a day, along the route toward the enemy. Time What happens Until 16:00 Members of both sides vote on the battle hour. 19:00 to 20:00 Raids can be launched. From 20:00 Sign up for your side's war warband with /warband list and /warband join. 21:00, 22:00 or 23:00 The battle starts. Each side's lives in a battle come from its regiments. After 20 minutes, a warband leader can /warband retreat, which ends the battle as a loss for that side. The faction that loses the war, and its subjects, pay the winner a quarter of their guilds' trade income for 10 days.

Only a faction leader can declare war, from the Diplomacy menu. Your faction's opinion of the target must be -50 or lower. No truce can stand between you. A truce lasts 10 days after a war ends. You need regiments that can attack, and staff must approve the declaration. You choose what you are fighting for, such as taking land, making them your subject, or pillaging.

Guilds can run a mercenary company and fight for other factions. A guild leader whose character has the Mercenary trait founds a company with /company found <name>. It costs 100 d from the guild bank and is ready a day later. Every mercenary needs the Mercenary trait. Each place in the company costs the guild 8 d a day, filled or not. The company leader writes a contract with /company draft, signs it, and sends it to a faction with /company offer <faction>. Factions browse companies with /mercenaries. To hire, their leader or a council member goes to the province of the company's guild capital and signs the contract there. Note Staff sometimes run battles outside wars. For those, make your own warband with /warband create, and its leader enters it with /battle join.

A short attack launched from a port or airport. During the raid hour, a faction leader at war can launch a raid from one of their own ports or airports. A port can raid an enemy port, an airport an enemy airport, and either one an enemy fort. Each side can only launch a few. The attackers have 60 seconds to join with /raid join <raid>, and the raid then lasts 10 minutes.

The leader keeps regiments from the Military menu, paid each day from the faction bank. Regiment Upkeep per slot Notes Professional Army 6 d Attacks and defends. Field Artillery 6 d Each slot keeps one artillery piece in the faction's vehicle pool. Militia 2 d Defends only. Levies None Raised from your subjects. New slots take hours to fill. The Military law changes which slots you get for free. If the faction bank can't pay, regiments shrink.

Right-click an idle Woodworking Station, choose a style, then a piece. Right-click the station with materials to add them one at a time. The title shows how many of each material type the piece still needs, but not which ones. Once all the materials are in, left-click the station with the tools. The title counts tools by group (see the table below), so full counts don't mean you used the right tools. Left-click with the Branding Tool to finish. The piece appears on top of the station. Right-click with it to see your progress, or sneak and left-click to cancel and get your materials back. Finishing shows your Recipe, Hits and Total percentages. Only exact work makes the piece: the right materials, and the right number of hits with each tool. If either is off, it is ruined and the materials are lost. If someone breaks the station mid-project, the materials go to whoever broke it.

Valewood, Runebark, Amberpine, Goldmaple, Silk. With the Herborist perk Tree Gatherer III, chopping any log or wood block can drop them. A Forestry node set to Rare Wood produces them too, once it has Diamond Axes or better. Spare wood sells at a Market Block.
